# Implementation status

This file records where the implementation stands, so that the work can be restarted from it.
The plan is Part G of DESIGN.md, in the spec repository (`../zed`). The repository layout is
in docs/layout.md.

## Current position

**2026-11-14 (AUDIT-p184).** 78 of 528 DESIGN steps are done (`PROGRESS.md`). dagview holds 2,307 items: 1,152 done, 1,083 unstarted, 39 active, 30 blocked by open author questions, 3 waiting; one component, no cycle; 337 ready. The bench split is finished, and the work follows the author's order P181: the FAIL-* rows first, then the completeness passes and the six handoff items, then the DAG. zed/IMPL.md section 7 in the spec repository has the same summary. The paragraphs below are history from 2026-11-05 onward.

**Zed₀ moved after the core (2026-11-05).** By the author's order, every core language feature goes
before Zed₀. `docs/plan_dag.md` had 826 items at that rework and has 815 items, 2685 edges and 89 levels after the later merges; S.1, which confirms
Zed₀, is at level 61. The merge took 938 findings from two audits of earlier
reviews and the Zig, Hydra and push-value studies. The stages before row S now include L1–L18,
the language parts of L19–L24 and the native path ZIR → MLIR → LLVM IR → x86-64. After row S come
the standard library's breadth (STD-full), the other back ends, microcontrollers, the editor, the
sketchbook, the libraries of L33 and OS portability. The Rust-hosted compiler keeps Cranelift; the
compiler written in Zed emits MLIR text (`zed/compiler/MLIR.md`, decision 9). The rework changed
plan, spec and docs only; no compiler code changed, and implementation stays held until the author
says go. Records: `wt/zed0-review/pass2/PLACEMENT.md`, `wt/review-audit/pass2/REPORT.md`. The DESIGN
fences changed, so test `l01_07` needs its expected output accepted at the next test build.

  every finding is listed in COMPLEXITY.md with its state. Fixed so far: the preimage transfer
  (exponential in `let` depth and guard nesting, now one computation per term and scope) and
  the projection (one split into conjunctions for all names, galloping bounds), the scope
  relation (shared conjuncts factored out of a join, at most 64 constraints and 64
  conjunctions kept), and the interval unions (forward images and operands capped to the piece
  limit, `cap` by a heap, `join` by a merge, `contains` by binary search), and the Omega test
  (dark shadow first, the real shadows alone before both recurse, a budget of 4,096 problems
  solved), and phase 1 of the store's iteration (head changes counted over the phase, and a
  component whose outside inputs did not change is skipped; nested loops cost linear work, where
  they were exponential in the depth), and the kernel's tuple and morphism parts (reduced
  ordered decision diagrams with shared nodes in place of clause lists, so a complement is
  linear; a union or intersection past 4,096 pairs of nodes keeps its operands, and emptiness
  past the budget answers "not shown empty"), and the split of a tuple clause (disjoint pieces,
  negated types disjoint from a piece passed over, 4,096 splits a query; unions of many types
  joined in pairs), and the formatter's blocks of one statement (rendered once, not twice
  per level), and defaults (a compound default is one definition its calls call, not a copy
  at each), the dependency order (a heap of ready items), the definedness `fix` (one shared map stamped by round; an entry postponed on a key waits on it; under pull, an undefined entry read is evaluated where it is read), the lattice `fix` (the iterates compared by their maps), strings (a join kept as its parts until read), recursive definitions (one pass for cycles, a shared body, names made when printed), listing a type's values (the cap checked before the product), provenance (each value walked once for a failure's origins, the terms of all facts in one walk), staging (the stage of a subterm read from an index of the term, names looked up in a map), the canonicalizer (every binder renamed in one walk, the facets sorted once), placing diagnostics (the line starts of a file found once, each place a binary search), the test runner (each row keyed and run under only the definitions it reaches, found from an index of the unit), the signature search (each run undone by a log of what it wrote; a nested function's signature found once per context, the context numbered and the memo hashed by it; a budget of 20000 checks of the outermost function's body, each counted at its own size, so the searches inside a function cost at most linear in its size however they nest),
  values (a family shared, not copied), the union of families (a persistent map, the smaller
  family inserted into the larger, since FAMILY-exact-nodes the kernel's own B-tree; `imbl` 7.0.2, MPL-2.0, accepted as a dependency for the other persistent maps: its terms
  apply to its own files only), the environment (a persistent map of the names in scope), provenance (the call
  sites and keypath in persistent vectors that fact addresses share), types (ordered by a
  hash of their contents kept in each; literal sets and atom maps persistent), and the kernel printer (a fit test that
  stops at the line's width). Scaling tests
  use `zed_tests::scaling::check` (n against 8n, under 10.5 times the work and the bytes since
  TESTS-scaling-limit-10_5, author 2026-11-13, which replaced the 13 of earlier that day; a ratio from 9 to 10.5 passes with a note naming the test), or `check_order`
  for work defined to be of order n^k (under 10.5 × 8^(k−1), `scaling::limit`); a test over the limit is ignored with its owner row. Work is user-mode instructions
  from the hardware counter, one run of each size after a warm-up at n, one measurement (TEST-scaling-runs), and a second run at 8n, the least of the two taken, only when the first is over the limit (FAIL-scaling-cold-8n-bytes); with no counter
  (`perf_event_paranoid` above 2, or a VM with no PMU) it is the task clock, the processor time of the thread and the threads it starts, and a
  test allows twice the limit and fails only when three measurements in a row are over; with `perf_event_open` refused the check stops with its own error. That is Linux; on macOS work is
  the process's instructions (`proc_pid_rusage`, else its cycles) and on Windows its cycles
  (`QueryProcessCycleTime`), with tests run one at a time; those paths are compiled, not run (PERF-portable). Every test run is capped at 64 GB, half the machine.

| T14-heap | done | `zed-rt/src/heap.rs`. A freed cell goes on a free list and the next allocation takes it; a cell word carries the cell's generation above a 40-bit index, so a word used after its cell was freed is reported even when the cell is taken again, and a cell freed in its last generation is retired. `try_inc` checks the generation and the count (`checked_add`, its own message); `inc` keeps its signature for `hooks.rs`, keeps an error and the next `dec` returns it, so `rt_inc` should call `try_inc` (T14-hooks). Matching reads the parts of a cell or a constant in place; a constant's parts enter the table once, together, the first time they are read, and the empty tuple and each bare atom have one entry. `Lit` compares part by part against the word, a string's length first; `is` reads a constant or a kernel value in place. `value` reads a cell held more than once once. `release_one` assigns kept paths to parts in one pass. The decided free list for `vals` is not done: a VAL word has no count and is copied freely, so nothing says when an entry is free; the table now grows with what a run reads, not with how often. The O(depth²) of R3 had already gone with T14-value (the scaling test passes on main). Tests: `l01_36_cranelift::reuse` (12), three scaling tests in `l01_36_cranelift::scaling` (n and 8n, power 1), two unit tests. Ordering two numbers that agree in many leading bits (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `min`, `max`, and a family's key order) asks before each precision of the bounds and before the near-tie build, and stops the run with `KernelError::OrderTooLarge` or `KeyOrderTooLarge`; `f64` of a number near a rounding boundary stops with `RoundTooLarge`, and a literal so near one is a compile error. `Rat::try_cmp` is the fallible order; `Ord` records a refusal while an evaluator run is active (`num::Watch`, a thread-local) and gives a total order on the normal forms meanwhile. Equality compares normal forms; when a prime the other operand keeps divides a coefficient, the copy that moves it out asks first (`EqualityTooLarge` for `==` and `!=`). The order of two plain rationals asks for its cross products. `String` of a tuple, keypath, atom or family sums the length of its whole text over every occurrence, a shared part's length read once, reserves that block and, with it held, asks for the widest number's build and the copy into the value; a number too large to build is `NumberTooLarge`, a text too large `TextTooLarge`. Tests `l01_17_value_representation::memory_check`: each refusal in a child process under a lowered `RLIMIT_AS` (which found three unasked copies of the operand, now removed), the same operations with memory given, and two scaling tests at power 1. Numbers of two kinds are ordered with the wide one borrowed, `int`, `rat` and `abs` share a wide number's digits, `-` and `abs` ask before copying one, and a refused equality in `match`, in a lattice `fix` and among a family's leaves has its own error. COMPLEXITY.md K30 (repairs 3 to 5). RAT-checked (K30 repair 9): `Rat::mul` and `Rat::div` ask first and return `Result`, `*`, `/` and `shl` refused with `NumberTooLarge` (`l01_17_value_representation::products`); a rounding round asks `32k` bits, not `16k`, below which a literal near a rounding boundary aborted the compiler, and that compile-time error is tested at +32 and +48 MiB (`memory_check`). RAT-asks (K30 repair 10): `to_integer`, the kept-power sum, `Rat::pow` of a wide base and a number's text ask 8 times their measured sizes (peaks 4.5 to 6.1 times); reading a decimal or other literal and `int(s)` and `rat(s)` ask first; the checker and elaborator read a literal's digits where they are, and a literal too long to read is one error at it; every refusal names the memory asked in bytes (`l01_17_value_representation::asks`). Open (item RAT-asks-rest): the compiler's serialization of a number; the lexer's and the AST's copies of a literal's text ask for nothing; `Text::flat` before `int(s)`, `rat(s)` and `f64(s)`; `mutate.rs`'s message, which prints the literal; and `check::menu` (LIT-plain), which copies a refused-carrier literal's text into its message up to four times. |

Load, check and batch give the same message (`l01_23_subtyping::bound_paths`, `l01_29_diagnostics::batch`). Elaboration no longer stops at a failed bound, so `x is (#a .. #b -> int)` now also reports that `is` cannot test a function type. (2) A rejection whose check the kernel refused now names the cause with `Ty::refused`: the overload message "does not take", in both its forms (no arrow meets the argument, `refused_among`; no arrow is left), the literal failure and the need-result check (`check_on`). A decided failure is unchanged: an arrow that some argument fails by a decided check gives no cause (`refusals::an_overload_rejected_by_a_decided_check_names_no_cause`). So the refused cases are tested through `check::operator` with kernel types: the seven-box cover (`TupleSplit`) and a morphism (`NoWitness`) on `neg`, `+`, `<` and `!` (`refusals::an_overload_whose_check_was_refused_says_why`). The decided cases are tested end to end. A literal against a tuple or morphism part is always decided, because a scalar never meets one. Choice: per-thread counts that a new thread takes from its parent, not one count for the process, because the tests of one binary run beside each other and a process count mixes their bytes. `zed-alloc-count` defines its own `pthread_create` (std starts every thread by it; it calls the C library's, found by `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)`), which gives the new thread an `Arc<Count>` holding its parent's; an allocation adds to its thread's count and each ancestor's (the chain is as deep as the nesting of thread starts). Each bounded variable is bounded on the outermost signature of its clause whose arrows name it, the one a call binds it in: resolve requires every use to lie in one outermost function type of the clause, and `check::Denote` reads the type from the top down, each use recording its bound on that function type, so the cost is linear however deeply clauses nest. Diagnostics, each with its span and a note: an unbounded name is a type variable of no clause (as before), a bound on a variable the type does not hold, a variable bounded twice (in one clause or in two), a bound that is not a union of carriers, a variable used outside a function type or in two function types of its clause, and an `is` test of a bounded type (elab: a test has no call to choose a carrier). The formatter writes the clause at level 0, below arrows; the checker prints the clause after a bounded signature and `check::read::parse_type` reads printed types through the AST. Six grammar cases (393 cases in all). An unbounded name inside a clause gets a note naming the innermost clause. Passing a bounded function where a function type is expected (`ty::fits_sig`): the expected type's bounded variables are renamed apart and held rigid, each standing for every carrier of its bound, so the result does not depend on variable names and two types that use one name are not confused; a function of one carrier, `(x: int) -> int`, is the function `(x: T) -> T for T in int`. A bounded variable that no parameter holds is fixed by no argument, so it stands for the union of its bound's carriers at a call (`close`), in a fit of a passed function on both sides (`fits_in`: such a variable of the expected type is not held rigid, and one of the passed function stays unbound after its parameters), and in the check of a lambda's result (`fit_lambda`); before repair 1, `() -> T for T in int \| f64` did not fit itself and `() -> 1` was refused there. The type printer is linear (COMPLEXITY.md F66; it was quadratic in depth on main). Tests `l01_26_type_resolution::bounds` (26): parse, round trip, accepted and refused calls, one carrier, two variables, nested clauses, printed types read back, the one-tuple `(T,)` and `L .. U -> V` read by the checker, a wider bound passed where a narrower one is expected (accepted) and the reverse (refused), renamed equal bounds, a one-carrier function passed as bounded, a result-only variable (passed as itself, as a narrower function, as a lambda, and refused outside its bound or with a wider one), and functions whose parameters are functions. Only five carriers exist, so scaling is measured in the number of bounded variables and of nested clauses, not of carriers in one bound. Scaling (COMPLEXITY.md F65): `many_bounded_variables_scale`, 800 and 6,400 bounds, 8.0 times; old per-variable argument scan in `apply_one` and `refuses` (from main) 28.3 times, fixed; `nested_bounds_clauses_scale`, 400 and 3,200 nested clauses, passes; the old walk of each clause's whole type 36.0 times (26.6 at 200 and 1,600, new code 8.9). Repair 3: `fits_in` no longer walks each signature's parameters or rewrites the expected signature at each depth; `Sig::held` is set when the signature is built and each side is read through a persistent map (`ty::Env`), so passing a function type nested d deep costs O(d) (COMPLEXITY F65: 8.1 and 8.2 times at 400 and 3,200 deep, plain and bounded; 26.6 and 59.0 times before). Not done: a bound on a declaration's own parameter types (`f(x: T for T in int) = x` is refused as standing outside a function type); a passed function whose own bounded variable occurs only under a function-typed parameter (`((x: U) -> U) -> U for U in int \| f64` where the same type with `T` is expected) is refused, soundly but needlessly, since `fits_sig` binds no variable of the outer function inside a nested function type; `Denote` does not record a bound on a variable that occurs only in a range's lower end, so that the printed type reads back; an inferred bound with the bit for values of no carrier prints as `for T in int \| other values` (`ty::mask_text`, from main), which is not user-writable syntax; the printer writes a nested bounded parameter with doubled parentheses, `((((x: T) -> T for T in int)) -> U for U in bool)`, which reads back but is redundant |

| JIT-reloc | merged and pushed (e408858b, rebased on main 43b7cdb5, and the commit that records this) | `l01_36_cranelift::table::bare_values_made_and_dropped_scale` panicked once under load in cranelift-jit `compiled_blob.rs:172`, `TryFromIntError(PosOverflow)`. That line applies `Reloc::X86PCRel4`, which non-position-independent x86-64 code emits only for the address of a symbol of the module itself: the `lea` in `codegen::Gen::root` that takes each lambda entry's address for `rt_register`. cranelift-jit's `SystemMemoryProvider` maps code one piece at a time, so the root and an entry can lie more than 2 GiB apart when other mappings land between them (inferred: another test thread's `Stack`, as large as memory; 0 of 21 runs of the l01_36 group at load 42 to 63 reproduced it by chance). Fix (`zed_native::run_in`): the JIT builds position-independent code on x86-64, as cranelift-jit's own default does. Every symbol address is then loaded through `X86GOTPCRel4`, which cranelift-jit turns into a `lea` when the symbol is within 2 GiB and otherwise into a load from an entry it adds at the end of the same allocation, and calls out of reach go through jumps added there, so no relocation depends on where the pieces lie. Rejected: one region reserved up front (`ArenaMemoryProvider`), since its size is a cap. Test: the unit test `placement::code_runs_with_its_functions_more_than_2_gib_apart` runs two lambdas, at both opt levels, with a memory provider that puts every allocation in its own 4 GiB slot; on the old flags it panics at `compiled_blob.rs:172:80` with the reported error, and passes with the fix. The 31 scaling checks of l01_36 give the same ratios with and without the change (within 0.1; e.g. n lambdas 8.05 and 8.05). Now `Ck::called` resolves the callee as `call` and `member_end` do (a name, or a member `x.r` / `x?.r`, bound to one binder whose type is one function, declared or a value) and gives the receiver, which `outside_arrow` puts in the first parameter, as `call_sig` does (with no atom for `?.`, which passes the receiver's atoms by), and which `outside_of` passes on as a part. Tests: `l01_16_elaboration::handled::a_method_call_passes_its_receiver_as_the_first_argument` (8 programs; red before green: the four method forms with the arrow selection failed on the branch before the fix, `method_handles_then_passes_on` first), two scaling tests (F75). Left open, non-blocking: the second arrow's result holds `#_` rather than the argument's own atoms. Repair 5 (verify 5, blocking): a method call without parentheses, `x.r`, `x.r.r` and `{ d = x else ""; x.r }`, gave `g` one arrow, and `g(" a ")` at a `Lines` port was rejected; so were `ap(r, x)` through a higher-order `ap(positional f, positional v) = f(v)` and the computed callee `(if true { r } else { r })(x)`, all of which ran on main. `outside_arrow` read the arrow selection from the callee as written, and these callees are not among those it reads. Now each call inside a function with a widened parameter records the loose atoms it gives from outside (`Ck::tried`): when an argument holds a loose atom, the call is applied once more with each such argument cut to its atoms from outside (`Ck::outside_args`, `Ck::try_outside`, an undo-log trial like those of `Ck::repairs`), and the trial's result atoms are recorded; otherwise the call records its own result atoms. A call of a value of several functions joins the records of each; a call of a type variable or a dynamic value records unknown, so all its atoms. The check of a need replayed at a call (`replaying`) records nothing, since its calls are not in the text. `outside_of` takes the record for a call or a member; `outside_arrow` is gone. A bare member `x.trim` of a prelude word takes the word's rule, as `trim(x)` does. Tests: `l01_16_elaboration::handled::a_method_call_passes_its_receiver_as_the_first_argument` (+4: `x.r`, `x.r.r`, `x.r` after a binding, `x.trim`) and `a_function_value_called_with_a_handled_parameter_gives_a_string_for_a_string` (new, 3: `ap(r, x)`, the computed callee, a wrapper `g` over `ap` that handles nothing); red before green: both tests failed at their new rows on the branch before the fix. Not fixed, present on the branch since its first commit and not on main: inside a handler, a lambda passed through a higher-order function, `ap((positional y) -> trim(y), x)`, is rejected ("`f` does not take (#_)"), since a need checked at a call has no argument span and so no rule 6 pass-by; main ran it because there `x` held no atom, and main rejects the same call on `stdin[2]` directly. Recorded as ISSUE1-lambda-need. Now pass-by is per atom: the atoms every arrow omits pass by, the rest stay in the argument and run the body, and `Info::passes` records the set each argument passes (`Ck::refused`, `Ck::pass_at`; the elaborator tests the argument with `is` that set before the call, `elab::walk::pass_end`). Blocking 2 (ISSUE1-lambda-need): `ap((positional y) -> trim(y), x)` inside a handler, alone or after `d = x else ""`, was rejected on the branch and ran on main. Of the two choices, (a) pass the refused atoms by at the higher-order call and (b) keep `x` unwidened, this repair takes (a), which follows rule 6 per atom: a need replayed at a call records the atoms the lambda refuses (`Ck::need_passed`), and the call that gave the lambda passes them by at the argument whose parameter holds the need's type variables (`Ck::pass_needs`); an atom that no argument of the call gives is still rejected (`ap(f) = f(#foo)`: "`f` does not take (#foo)"), and a need checked at a function's own body with no such call is rejected as before. Behavior change: `ap((positional y) -> trim(y), stdin[2])` now runs and gives the atom (main rejected it). Tests: `l01_16_elaboration::handled` (+4: the is-only, pattern-else and declared bodies at a `Lines` port, an omitted atom passing by beside a tested one, four lambda forms through `ap` and `ap2`, the rejected `f(#foo)`); red before green: on the branch before the fix the first five probe programs were rejected (and the declared one and the direct `ap` on main). Scaling: `many_calls_passing_some_atoms_of_their_argument_by_scale` and `a_chain_of_functions_each_testing_an_atom_of_its_own_scales` (F76). Still open, non-blocking: the second arrow's result holds `#_` rather than the argument's own atoms. |

| AND-fns | merged and pushed (240bfcc6, 42b40566, cb992e04, rebased on main 6ba12c8a, and the commit that records this; spec 5be8ce5, e7b9d75) | COMPLEXITY.md F82. `((x: int) -> String) & ((x: f64) -> String)` read back by `parse_type` as one signature of two arrows, as DESIGN.md sec:type_language point (2) says ("it is notation for that list"); before, `Denote` met the two function types as a meet, and the printed overload did not read back as itself. The rule the spec branch adds: the arrows share one parameter list (count, and the name of each parameter a call names; a positional or unnamed parameter's name is not compared) and one set of bounds; `resolve` and `parse_type` reject an intersection of function types that differ there, two operands that bound one variable by different carriers, and a bounds clause around an intersection that is an operand of another. An overload in parentheses inside another, `(A & B) & C`, is read as `A & B & C` (repair 2: before, a nested intersection was joined by arity alone, so a differing parameter name was dropped without an error, and a second bound of one name replaced the first). A mixed intersection (`int & f`) keeps the meet. A slot written as an overload takes each arrow (`l01_26_type_resolution::fits`). `fits_in` tries an equal arrow first by hash; arrows that differ still cost n·m (open: AND-fns-fit). Found, not changed: `inc(x) = x + 1` passed to an overload slot is read as `(x: int) -> int` and rejected, as on main |

Now an `ArrowIndex` of the argument's read arrows, built once per call after the equal-arrow lookup, gives each slot arrow its candidates: per parameter position, a posting list of arrow indices for each carrier and each bare atom name the parameter type offers (`Type::atom_names`, new in zed-kernel), and the arrows whose parameter type is open (a variable, dynamic, cofinite atoms, or no such parameter). The shortest list the slot arrow's parameters need is merged with the open list and filtered by the other needed keys; `arrow_fits` runs on these in order and stops at the first that fits. The verdict is the old one, since a parameter type that offers no piece of a needed key cannot hold it; the differential test `check::ty::tests::the_index_of_arrows_gives_the_verdict_of_every_pair` checks it against the all-pairs search on random overloads (1.2 s). Rule 6 of sec:type_resolution types an application of an overload region by region of the argument, so `((x: int) -> String) & ((x: bool) -> String)` fits the slot `(x: int \| bool) -> String`; `fits_in` refused it. Now, when no single arrow fits a slot arrow, `check::ty::covered` accepts it when, at one parameter j, its parameter lies within the union of parameter j of the arrows that hold its other parameters and return within its result. `ArrowIndex` files each arrow also under the rarest carrier or atom name its result needs, so the candidates of a slot arrow, single or together, are the arrows whose result keys lie within its result's. This is the item's description; rule 6 is wider, and the check refuses three cases rule 6 accepts, named in the tradeoff comment at `covered`: a cover split across two or more parameters (DNF tautology, coNP-complete), arrows whose parameter j holds a variable or the unknown, and overlapping arrows whose results only intersect within the slot's result, as `((x: int) -> String \| #a) & ((x: int) -> String \| #b)` for `(x: int) -> String` (the all-subsets condition). Tests: the formerly ignored `l01_26_type_resolution::fits::an_overload_that_covers_a_slots_parameter_only_together_fits` (with a run-through, a positional and a three-arrow variant), `arrows_that_cover_together_must_each_return_within_the_slots_result`, `arrows_that_cover_only_across_two_parameters_or_by_intersected_results_are_refused`; the differential tests, renamed `check::ty::tests::the_index_of_arrows_gives_the_verdict_of_every_set_of_arrows{,_on_wider_shapes}`, compare with the all-pairs search and a search over every nonempty set of at most 10 arrows (6.2 s together). The formerly ignored probe, now `l01_26_type_resolution::bench::scaling::passing_an_overload_whose_arrows_share_a_parameter_piece_scales`: 7.9 times the bytes and the work at n = 100 and 800, load 9 to 10 (57.6 before; 24 allowed). Negative control, not committed: the result index skipping arrow 0 fails both differential tests and 15 of the 181 tests of l01_26. Not fixed: arrows that share one piece of both the slot's parameter and its result stay O(n·m) (tradeoff at `every_arrow_fits`). No spec change. Verify (AND-fns-rule6:verify#1): fixed the soundness hole of a variable inside a tuple at the cover parameter and the cost of the square of the width (COMPLEXITY.md F82); added the order and wider-shape index checks, two scaling tests and the function-type refused case; the refused cases still share the message that the function is not taken, a defect for AND-fns-rule6b. |

| ZIR-family-key | merged and pushed (the commit that records this) | COMPLEXITY.md Z20. The ZIR text and binary readers built a family literal by `Family::of`, which panics when a key repeats (family.rs, `expect`), while a repeated atom field already gave an error. Now they do (`Ty::function_in`), `Ck::data` gives the classes in payloads their need, and a `==`, `!=` or `String` refusal derives from the operand, so it shows where the function came from (a new note, "this atom `#a` with its payload"). Tests: `l01_17_value_representation::equality` (4 new), `l01_29_diagnostics::derivations` (1), `l01_26_type_resolution::held_functions` (2, one scaling). Open: (1) `held_wide` exists only on wt/atom-payload-sub and needs the same payload walk when both merge; (2) `Row::open` ignores variables in payloads, so `f(positional x) { return #a(x), 1; }` then `p = f(x); p == p` in another function, called with a lambda, is still accepted (ledger ATOM-payload-open); (3) atoms nested directly in atoms are O(n^2) in the checker, before this item too; fixed by ATOM-nested-sq (F106) |
| OMEGA-cycle-growth | merged and pushed (the commit that records this) | Repair found by NAME-orbit-test. The 4-cycle `x0 >= x1 >= x2 >= x3 >= x0` in `[-1, 1]^4` with `1 <= x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 <= 3` was refused `Growth`: `Omega::run` entered its loop with 14 rows and took no step (every elimination had fill 10, four live variables, no inexact variable), and the box stage found neither emptiness nor a point. Now `Omega::cycles` runs once, before the first step that is not an equality: the rows `x - y + k >= 0` with `k <= 0` (and one-variable rows through a node for zero) are edges, and the rows of each strongly connected component (Tarjan, `utvpi::components`, now `pub(super)`) become equalities, solved as those of the input; an edge of weight above zero in a component shows the system empty. O(m log m + n). The orbit test now asserts `Ok(false)`; new tests `l01_38_presburger::omega::a_cycle_of_rows_makes_its_variables_equal` and `l01_38_presburger::scaling::a_cycle_of_rows_scales` (512 and 4,096 variables: 9.4 times the instructions, 8.0 times the bytes, load 57 to 59). Controls, not committed: the search disabled fails all three tests with `Growth`; the components found again for each equality fails the scaling test (38.2 times the bytes). Not found, recorded as a complexity tradeoff (COMPLEXITY.md OMEGA-cycle-growth): zero-sum cycles with weights of both signs, and cycles that form only after a step. |

| FLOAT-minmax | merged and pushed (the commit that records this) | Author decision 2026-11-04, DESIGN.md sec:reduction item 5: `min` and `max` on floats are IEEE 754-2019 `minimum` and `maximum`; a NaN in either position gives the NaN, `min(-0.0, 0.0)` is `-0.0` in both orders, `clamp(x, lo, hi) = max(lo, min(x, hi))`. | FLOAT-tie-read | done (test and STATUS only) | Why a float tie prints the larger magnitude (DESIGN.md sec:reduction item 1, "Of two shortest digit strings equally near the value, printing takes the one of larger magnitude"), read in the std source of the toolchain in use, rustc 1.99.1 (Fedora; the files moved to `library/core/src/num/imp/flt2dec/strategy/`, logic unchanged from 1.93.0). `zed_kernel::num::show_f64` takes its digits from `{:e}`, which calls `grisu::format_shortest`. Its `format_shortest_opt` ends in `round_and_weed`, which returns `None` (grisu.rs:442; 440 in 1.93.0) when the digits nearest `v` plus its error bound are not also nearest `v` minus it, as at an exact tie, and the fallback `dragon::format_shortest` decides: `if up && (!down \|\| *mant.mul_pow2(1) >= scale)` (dragon.rs:247; 245 in 1.93.0) rounds up when twice the remainder is at least the scale, so exactly one half goes up, in magnitude, since the sign is apart. Probe (RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP, `num_internals`, not committed): on 104,000 constructed ties `format_shortest_opt` returned `None` every time and Dragon gave the larger form every time; on 100,000 random floats Grisu succeeded on 99,596. Where ties are: `v = M * 2^-p` is halfway between `D * 10^-j` and `(D+1) * 10^-j` only when `M = K * 2^t`, `K` odd, `t = p - j - 1`, both read back when `10^j >= 2^p`, and they are the shortest only if `10^(j-1) < 2^p`; `0 <= t <= 51` then confines ties to `2^-23 <= \|v\| < 2^51`, in 52 of the 74 binades there; at a binade's lower end, where the float below is nearer, there is one more, `2^-25` (printed `...313e-8`, the larger; found at merge by a scan of every binade and every `t`, and checked on its own by the test). In units of `10^-j / 2`, `v` is `K * 5^j`, an odd multiple of 5, always 5 units from the nearest multiple of `10^-(j-1)`, so a binade has ties exactly when `2^p <= 10^j < 5 * 2^p`, and then every float `K * 2^t * 2^-p` in it is one; the test checks this rule on every sample. Test `l01_18_scalar_interpreter::floats::every_sampled_tie_prints_the_larger_magnitude` replaces the 8,000,000-sample program that was never in the repository: 1,000 draws from a fixed seed in each binade the condition allows, each checked in exact `u128` arithmetic (halfway, both neighbors read back, whether a nearest multiple of `10^-(j-1)` does, against the binade rule); 52,000 ties in 52 binades, each with both texts read back through `f64(s)` bit for bit and `String` printing `D+1` (and `-` before it for `-v`); 0.45 s, linear in the samples. Negative control, run once and reverted: `show_f64` rounding ties down fails this test (`1180954526937006.75` printed `...006.7`) and the 1666666666666669.25 test; the other 48 of l01_18 pass. Changed at merge: the halfway check read `K` from the sampler, odd by construction, so it could not fail; it now reads `M` from `v`'s bits, and a sampler built one below each tie fails it (it failed only the later read-back check before); the tie at `2^-25` was added; rounding ties down fails both the sampled ties and the `2^-25` check. Flaw named, not fixed: there is no rust-toolchain file, so the rule rests on std internals; this test is what would catch a change. An edit-script format for the query cache of L1.30, in `l01_30_queries/reuse.rs`: a script is text whose `%% step`, `%% write`, `%% replace` … `%% with` and `%% delete` lines edit a set of files, run with one database kept across the steps; after each step every unit's checks (verdicts and diagnostics, `test_in`) and the package's report, unit order and each unit's resolution (`unit::load`, every `.zed` file a root) equal a fresh database's. Check-only: no built program is compared. `every_answer_equals_a_fresh_databases` is now a script of the same six texts. Corner cases: a type error added then removed (the fixed text computes nothing and checks as before), a renamed definition (the importer is resolved again and reports the missing name, then follows), a changed import edge (an import added, moved to another unit with the first unit deleted, a cycle made and removed, an import of a missing unit); two malformed scripts stop with their own messages. A unit with imports is checked alone by `test_in`, which reports its imports as needing a manifest, so its own checks say little until a package test runner exists; the package's report and resolutions are what those steps compare. Scaling 8 and 64 steps: 7.2 times the instructions and the bytes (limit 24, load 49). Negative controls, run once and not committed: rows keyed by the check alone, without the definitions it reaches, fail 3 tests (2 of them scripts); a resolution keyed by its text alone, without its imports' exports, fails `a_renamed_definition` and `a_changed_import_edge` and no older `l01_30` test; a runner doing i fresh checks at step i fails the scaling test at 41.9 times the bytes. Rung 2 translates `a div n` and `a mod n` for a divisor `n` that is not a constant: quotient `q` and remainder `r` auxiliary, `a == n * q + r` with `n * q` a product atom (`Lin::product` now takes auxiliary variables as factors, through `presburger::Factor`), one disjunct per sign of `n` with `0 <= r <= \|n\| - 1`, and `q`, `r` free at `n == 0`. | T6-2sat | verified, ready for the batch merge on branch wt/t6-2sat (not merged) | COMPLEXITY.md K54. A tuple part that is a 2-CNF over two-valued components is decided by Tarjan's strongly connected components of its implication graph, in O(V + E) with an explicit stack, and recognized by structure: each open tuple type open on one component, each component cut into one piece and its complement, each clause of at most two literals (`types/empty.rs` `Searching::two_sat`, `read_two_sat`, `TwoSat::solve`; `Part::id` and `Bdd::id` in `bdd.rs`). `tuples_on` uses it before the per-length search, and `find_rep` takes the witness from it, the box cut to the pieces the solution chooses. The x_tail.rs cnf probe on main first: no refusal on r2, chain, chainsat or xorcycle (Search::refine, K35), but xorcycle cost about n^3.5 (22.8 s at 129 variables); after: 7.8 ms. Tests `l01_23_subtyping::two_sat` (9) and two kernel unit tests in `empty.rs`. Scaling (merge verification, orchestrator's decision): n is the type's size, of order the variables squared, so the chain, the open chain and the parity cycle run at 45 and 128 variables (types 8 times apart) within the standard 24; the search before this item is n^1.5 in the type and passes that too (22 times), so a fourth test measures the parity cycle by its variables, 11 and 88, within 24 (8.9 times; the control fails it at 446 times the bytes). Groups run, each under timeout 60: l01_23_subtyping (140 tests, by module) and its deep_search target (8), l01_22 (41) and l01_29 (133 and 1 ignored; both read emptiness and printed types), zed-kernel unit tests (88), all pass on the rebased tree, load 40 to 72; again at merge verification, with deep_types (20), load 35 to 41. No ZED_PORT_GAPS entry: plain vectors, maps and loops. |

Not done: `zedc test` prints rejection outcomes without addresses; `Package::report` and the refusals of `program()` print none; the address names only the top-level declaration, not a full keypath. Two files of one text have two addresses, any paths to one file one, hard links two; a tree copied elsewhere and run from the same place prints the same addresses, and running from another directory prints others (queued as DIAG-addr-root: the deterministic-checking rule asks for addresses that do not depend on where `zedc` runs). | DIAG-addr-root | merged and pushed in batch 35 (5fc72dd5, da6e94c6; `crates/zedc/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `place.rs`, `run.rs`, `suppress.rs`, `testing.rs`, `unit.rs`); spec 08a19a2 (DESIGN sec:diagnostics, no grammar change) | COMPLEXITY.md row DIAG-addr-root. | ISSUE1-tvar-else | committed on wt/issue1-tvar-else, not merged | COMPLEXITY.md row ISSUE1-tvar-else. From ISSUE1-else-atoms impl#1. `r(positional line, bump = 1) = (line else 0) + bump` inferred `(_, bump: int) -> int`, so `r(" a ")` checked and failed at run time with "type error: Add applied to". The cause was not the `else`: `Ck::apply_many` merged the paths `(int, int)` and (class, int) of the sum into one state, since both kept the int arrow, and dropped the second, which carried the class's restriction. States are now also keyed by `ClassAt`, the carriers each alive arrow allows where the class stands. The signature is `(int \| #_, bump: int) -> int` and `r(" a ")` is refused at the call. Tests: `handled::a_count_or_zero_plus_a_named_step_takes_the_step_s_carrier`, `handled::a_count_or_zero_plus_another_parameter_shares_its_carrier`, scaling `sums_of_a_line_or_a_count_check_in_linear_time`. Verification with the old `apply_many`: the first handled test and the scaling test's signature check fail (`(_, bump: int) -> int`); the second handled test passes on the old code too and guards the case with both parameters undeclared. The verifier reran the negative control (a copy of `Ck::seen` per `apply_many` call): 55.1 times the bytes, limit 24, load 27. `apply_many` is reached only by operators and prelude words of several arrows (a call of a user function of 6 arguments, each `(line else 0)`, does not reach it), so its states per call stay bounded (at most 3 measured) |

| LIST-xor-finite | merged and pushed in batch 27 (b47553d5; `crates/zed-kernel/src/types.rs`) | COMPLEXITY.md K69. `Type::each_value` gave `None` for two finite types: `((u, u),)`, `u = 0..8`, met with the exclusive or of `((int - (2k + 1), int),)` for `k < 3`, and the exclusive or of each such row met with the square first. `Type::boxes` gave each tuple type of an expression as a box. It now finds an expression's boxes from its operands' (`part_boxes`, two passes, each operand read once per sign by id, explicit stack): a union has the boxes of its two operands, a meet those of its one operand that has boxes, or, when both have, those of the operand with fewer boxes, each met with the join of the other's unless its columns are all finite; the complement is taken down by De Morgan's laws, so an exclusive or of finite types and a meet with a finite type are finite, and the boxes of an infinite complement are never built. Boxes are kept in persistent sets. Listing: `RowIndex::holds` no longer evaluates the whole part per candidate; the part is a `Graph` of its distinct lists and expressions, a union read by one union merged into it (and so meets), node values kept per class, and a candidate re-reads only the lists of its keyed rows and the nodes whose value changes; a tuple is tried once, in the first box that gives it (`HashSet` keyed by the numbers of its components, `Numbers`, replacing `BoxIndex`), a lookup in the tuple's length whatever the depth of its components. `meet_types` returns `x` for a meet with `top`, so a tuple type of `n` literals is found finite in constant time, not O(n). `Lits` orders by `==` first, which skips shared nodes, so the each-row shape with a side as wide as the rows is found finite in O(n log n) (was O(n²)). | TABLE-life | merged and pushed in batch 18 (2e0df7a3); no spec change | COMPLEXITY.md K66. The per-thread tables of treap nodes, list cells and exclusive ors (CHAIN-zip-size), and `rec.rs` `GROUPS` and `INSTANCES`, kept every entry for the life of the thread, and an expression and its complement held each other: a run of 2,048 independent checks left 167.4 MB allocated on the thread (about 81 KB a check). The tables now hold `Weak` entries that each node removes when dropped, and an expression and its complement hold each other one way only (`Expr::back`), so the same run leaves 0 bytes and the resident bytes stay at 9.5 MB. Ids stay unique and a live node is found again by the same id; a node made again after its drop has a new id and the same digest; a complement made again after its holder was dropped is made from the form it was written with (`Expr::source`): same structure and digest, so order and printed text do not depend on what was freed. Rows are kept in a weak table (`ROWS`), so equal rows alive together are one node. Tests `l01_22_type_representation::table_life` (bounded memory at n and 8n, scaling of a run by its length), `types::bdd::tests` (three lifetime tests), `types::rec::tests` (two). The meet scaling test of `types::bdd::tests` is unchanged: it had found its second list's rows again only through the nodes the immortal tables kept, and now finds them through `ROWS`. Open: a recursive instance is a strong cycle through its members' keys and unfoldings and is never freed (item REC-cycle); `Key::group` (from main) names a group by the address of its live `Env`, which is unique only while that instance lives. |

A due tree with neither, outside a whole-scope projection, is narrowed by `Scope::shortest`: the scope keeps a potential, repaired for the new edges by the Cotton–Maler 2006 Dijkstra on reduced costs (a negative cycle empties the scope), then the bounds move by Dijkstra from the changed names, O((names changed + their edges) log n) per test. Any other tree or a name with no interval falls back to the projection; the potential is set again from `presburger::satisfiable` only once per tree after a projection of every block (tradeoff comment at `Scope::reseed`; k `if`s each after an `if` on a sum, between rungs, 8.4 times the bytes at 40 and 320, no reseed). The same mix on a hole is 58.3 times, as at the base: pre-existing, in the projection of the holed tree. The ladder of k `if` statements is now order 1 in both orders (12.4 times the bytes at 40 and 320; 51.8 times with the new path off). Every reduce of the l01_39*, l01_38, l01_25 and zedc_preimage groups gave the same scope both ways (361 pieces, 0 mismatches, a temporary cross-check not committed). A prototype of the trivial-model report of DESIGN.md sec:theories item 3 over a small term language with `==`, `!=`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `!` and `.implies(..)`, until L22 parses law members. The fields split into groups linked by a common law; a field no law names is printed as free and not enumerated; the one-value model is checked once; each law is put in conjunctive normal form (writing it out is charged one step per comparison written by distributing an `\|\|` over an `&&`, against `BUDGET`, 2^20 steps, the stand-in for A54's compile-time budget that MIX-budget replaces; a law that reaches it is refused with a message naming the work limit and the repair: split it into laws whose `\|\|`s hold no `&&`s, or state it as a theorem with a proof); each group is searched with incremental arc consistency on the cubes of its comparisons and a union-find check of its clauses of several comparisons, run when one of their fields becomes fixed, and for one open field only on the comparisons that reach it. The default report lists up to two models per group and stops at the first choice that leads to no model, with the chain of laws that rule it out and the repair `@exhaustive`; `@exhaustive` lists every model. Checked against brute force on 4,000 random theories, with `!` and `.implies(..)` in their laws (all agree; 1,215 in the forest fragment with 0 dead ends, 525 of the other 2,785 with a dead end), on five theories written with `!` and `.implies(..)`, and on the corpus (Semigroup 4 models, Band 2, Codec 1, the identity twice; Monoid, NonCommRing, CommRing, Ring, NonTrivialRing, Group, Lattice and BooleanAlgebra none on two values, refuted before any choice; no dead end in the corpus). Hardness: `p(x, x) == x` makes a binary field one bit, so clause laws encode 3-SAT (300 random formulas, one model per satisfying assignment); `a != b \|\| b != c` laws on constants encode NAE-3SAT [Schaefer78] (the Fano plane: no model, 12 dead ends); an `\|\|` of `&&`s encodes 3-UNSAT in one law with no field, so such laws are coNP-complete to decide (`hardness::an_or_of_ands_is_refused`); dead ends on the pigeonhole formulas for 1 to 6 holes 0, 2, 9, 52, 375, 3,246; random 3-CNF at 5 clauses per variable, mean dead ends 6.6, 22.6, 101.6, 3,582.4 at 10, 20, 40, 80 variables. Open: an atom whose two sides share fields is cubic in the atom (C32 (1), TRIVIAL-shared-atom), pinned by `scaling::a_shared_field_atom_is_cubic` and left to the coordinator before the author. Answer: it matters, and the earlier explanation was wrong. The join's relation is the exact disjunction of the sides' relations; what is not exact is the projection of a core of two or more disjunctions, which is done one disjunction at a time (S16). A join whose free conjuncts hold neither side's adds a disjunction to the core, and the leaf's bound widens (-4 against -3); new test `a_join_that_adds_a_second_disjunction_to_the_core` fails on the mutant. Also fixed a bug on main cbfd0720: a join whose cases test a name outside the star, such as `(z >= 0 && n + m <= -7) \|\| (z < 0 && n - m >= -30)`, drops the star, and the stale leaf was never settled (-11 against -10). The join now diffs the stars and classes of each side against the join's (persistent maps, O(changes · log n)) and settles the leaves removed or moved; test `a_case_that_tests_another_name_drops_the_star`. An operation on literals alone keeps, at `rat`, its value, or for a power whose base is not `0`, `1` or `-1` a range read without computing the power (a power of a text value at `\|k\| >= 2` is at least or at most its square, a power of a range its range's ends; a negative exponent inverts), so `(2r/3r)^-2`, `1r / (2r/3r)`, `1r / (3r^2 + 1r)` and `1r / (2r^2 - 3r)` have no `#divByZero` and are written to a port with no `else`. Decisions made without asking (coordinator's rules 1-5 followed): ranges and not values, since DESIGN asks a check linear in the text and `3r^200000` has 95 000 digits; squares only of values of the text (squaring range ends doubles them at each nested power); value typing narrows inside an existing arrow only (`4r ^ 0.5r` stays rejected); integer exponents stay `int`, so `(3/2)^-2` is rejected at `/` with the exact `(3r/2)^-2` among the fixes, and `2 ^ -1` keeps its menu with `2r ^ -1`. Fixed on the way, unsound before: a literal with no suffix compared with a `rat` or `f64` name was read as the `int` it is alone, so `if r == 0 { x / r + 1r } else { 0r }` with `r: rat` gave `(x: rat, r: rat) -> 0r`, dropping the arm `f(x: 1r, r: 0r)` runs, and `r == 1 + 1` did the same; `Ck::term` now reads the literal at the carrier it adopts (`Ck::carrier_here`), and `Scope::atom_names` does not meet a name holding no `int` with an `int` literal. Tests in `tests/steps/l01_26_type_resolution/divisors.rs`: three new tests and a scaling test (7.98 times the work and the bytes at n = 100 and 800). Open: `-r != 0r` and a name bound to `0r` (`z = 0r; r != z`) do not narrow; `r > 1r { x / (r - 1r) }` keeps `#divByZero`, since only `0r` is taken out, not an interval; `x / r` under `r == 0r` gives no "always fails" error, unlike `x div d` under `d == 0` |

| LIT-rat-int-op-exponent | merged and pushed (36c4da004 to c7bd75a0b); no spec change: DESIGN sec:lexical already gives a `rat` base any `int` exponent, and the plan text "no integer literal removes rat" was a paraphrase, corrected in rows POW-top-body-agree and LIT-rat-decimal-exponent | COMPLEXITY.md LIT-rat-int-op-exponent. In a body `2^(1 + 1) + 2r`, `2^(1 + 1) == 4r`, `(1/2)^(3 - 1) * 2r` and `2r * 2^(2^100 - 2^100 + 3)` were rejected; the top level gave `6r`, `true`, `1r/2r`, `16r`. Cause: in a body the exponent `(1 + 1)` is a generic class that `apply_many` joined to the base's, and `^` has no arrow (rat, rat). Now, in `binary_op`, an exponent that is an operation on integer literals alone stands for its value as a bare literal exponent at its span (`Ck::int_exponent_at`, memoized in `Ck::int_exponents`); elaboration follows it by that span (`follow` in zedc-elab), without which `g(positional x) = 2^(1+1) + x; g(0.5f64)` stopped with "`^` applied to `f64`, `int`". Menus: the `rat` fix leaves an `int` exponent as it is (`unreached` at `rat`), so `y = 2 ^ (1 + 1) / 3` offers `y = 2r ^ (1 + 1) / 3` beside `f64`; the soundness note gives the exponent's value ("this `-` gives -2"). An exponent whose value is no exact `f64`, as `2 ^ 100 - 1`, removes `f64` in a body as the same value written as one literal does. Tests: l01_26a `top_body_agree` (the brief's 4 lines and 9 corners in top level, body and block, a parameter case, 5 rejections that stay; 4 tests red on origin/main before the fix; `0.5^(1 + 1)`, `2^(1 + 1) < 0.5` and `0.5^(2^100 - 2^100 + 3)` now leave `rat` among the carriers at the top level as `0.5^2` does, so they are rejected in both places where the top level read them at `f64`); benchmark l01_26a `bench::nested_int_operation_exponents_are_read_in_linear_time` at n = 2000 and 16000: 8.00x instructions, 7.99x bytes, 1x 0.33 s (n = 3000 came near the 20 s piece limit); negative control without the memo did not end in 60 s at n = 2000 (not committed); expectations in l01_26 adoption and soundness, l01_26a fixes and lazy_carrier, l01_29 fold_machine and too_large (`this ^ gives 2^70`) updated to the DESIGN reading. l01_26, l01_26a, l01_29, l01_30, zedc_check, zedc_elab and l01_10, l01_17, l01_18, l01_19*, l01_21, l01_23, l01_25, l01_27, l01_38, l01_39*, l03_09, l25_08, m0_03, m0_05, m0_06 pass but for pieces over the 20 s limit that time out on origin/main too (l01_26a lit_branch_ops, same instruction count; l01_38 q1_local and names 105–108; l01_17, deep_search and l01_23 refusals pass alone); fmt and clippy clean. Open: in a body an inexact literal exponent removes `f64` but not `f32` from the carriers listed (`2 ^ 1267650600228229401496703205375 / 3` lists `f32 | rat`), as before this change. |

| FAIL-values-cast-negzero | merged and pushed (the commit that marks the row Done); no spec change | Found by TEST-complete-values. Cause: `crates/zed-kernel/src/words.rs` cast a finite float to `f32` or `f64` through its exact rational (`x.exact()`, then `exact_f32` or `exact_f64`), and a rational has no sign of zero, so `f32(-0.0f64)` and `f64(-0.0f64)` gave `0.0`. Fix: `f64` of an `f64` is the value itself; `f32` of a finite `f64` is `f as f32` when it widens back to `f`, `#overflow` past the largest `f32`, else `#inexact`, all `O(1)`. Tests: `l01_18_scalar_interpreter::cast_negzero` (the row test, red before the fix, and its neighbors), kernel `casts_between_number_kinds` (zeros, subnormals, the `f32` range boundary) |
