## Decisions made

- Toolchain: Fedora's rustc and cargo 1.99.1, edition 2024. CI uses the stable toolchain.
- Cargo's target directory is `build/cargo`, set in `.cargo/config.toml`.
- Language tests: `tests/steps/<step>/`, all in one test binary. Unit tests of internal
  functions: `#[cfg(test)]` beside the code.
- Fences and grammar (SPEC-standalone, 2026-11-13; supersedes SPEC-no-copies and
  SPEC-no-verbatim): this repository builds and passes its tests from a fresh clone with no
  access to the private spec. What it needs of the spec is copied by the hand-run command
  `cargo run -p zed-tools --bin sync -- <spec dir>` (or `$ZED_SPEC_DIR`): the grammars, the
  desugaring rules and the table of words into `zed/grammar/` (zedc-syntax embeds `syntax.peg`
  with `include_str!`, so no build script reads the spec), and the `zed` fences, the text fences,
  the rejection rows and the kernel rule names into `zed/fences/`. Only grammar rules, fences with
  a one-line header, row names and test programs are copied, never prose. `sync --check` writes
  nothing and exits nonzero naming each copy that differs; it also runs the checks that need the
  spec's prose (the prelude laws against docs/mathlib-study.md, the build-mode table, the `sec:`
  citations). No build and no test runs `sync`, and only `sync` and its unit test name
  `ZED_SPEC_DIR`. The ✗ variants are fixtures again (`zed/fences/variants/*.zed`), each compared
  with its fence by `zed_tests::fences::disagreements`; `zed/fences/variants.txt` is gone.
- No Python (the author's instruction, 2026-10-31): the repositories hold Rust and Zed only, plus
  `tools/dagview` in TypeScript. The tools are the
  binaries of the crate `crates/zed-tools`, each taking the spec directory as its first
  argument, run as `cargo run -q -p zed-tools --bin TOOL -- ../zed ...`: `check`, `cases`,
  `fences`, `fuzz`, `layer`, `ring`, `audit`, `progress`, `cite`, which checks the
  spec's `sec:` labels and step ids cited in DESIGN.md and here, and `plan`, which checks
  `docs/plan_dag.md` and takes no spec directory (`plan --fix` first rewrites its level column
  and the counts of its first paragraph from the needs). They share the grammar rules
  and the engine of `zedc::parse`. The corpus references are the crate `zed/corpus/ref`
  (`ref NN INPUT`, `ref --write`), which depends on no compiler crate; the step test
  `m0_04_corpus_references` compares every `.out` with it in the local suite, so CI needs no
  other language.
- Reference 13 stores only the nodes on edges, in a hash map from the node number to a slot in
  the parent and size arrays, so input of 20 bytes can name a node of any size; components are
  the node count less the merges. Reference 14 is O(n log n) by a Delaunay triangulation in exact
  integers, and its O(n²) form is the test oracle (COMPLEXITY.md F39, plan node P14-MST, done).
  Of two shortest digit strings equally near a float, printing takes the larger magnitude:
  Rust's `{:e}` does (8,000,000 ties sampled in [2^50, 2^51) all rounded up;
  `core::num::flt2dec::strategy::dragon` rounds up when twice the remainder is at least the
  scale), and the spec now says so (sec:reduction). Why, read in the std source, and the test
  that now holds the rule in place of that sampling program: Steps row FLOAT-tie-read.
- The tools (DART-RS). A hole failure gives the hole parser's position in the hole's own tokens.
  `progress` with no sec:steps refuses with exit status 1. Identifiers are ASCII
  names, as the compiler reads them (NAME-ascii-only). A duplicate rule across the syntax and
  documentation grammars is an error, `audit` passes on the exit status of `layer`, a crash
  exits 1, `check` reads fences from its spec argument, and `fuzz` computes depths by Knuth's
  generalization of Dijkstra's algorithm. A spec with fewer than three `peg` fences is
  refused by every tool. A failure is a one-line message, not a stack trace.
- The references: on a cycle, 15 and 27 give an error. The second rewrite (04, 07, 15, 27, 31
  and 02, 05, 16) agrees with the first on 13800 random and mutated inputs and 1800 well-formed
  typechecker inputs.
- No reference recurses on its input now, and the tools parse with the iterative machine of
  `zedc::parse`, generic over its input, so `on_large_stack` is gone from both crates and a deep
  program runs through `ring`, `layer` and `check` on a 2 MiB stack. The tools still recurse over
  the grammar's text (`Reader`, `Expr`'s `Drop` and `Clone`, `fuzz`'s walks of rules), which is
  bounded by the nesting of the spec's own rules, not by a program. A `%` in the grammar copies
  its operand, so nested `%` doubles per level; the spec does not nest it. Reference 13 allocates by a node number in its input, and 16 and 26
  loop over a tick or step count in their input: their cost follows a value, not a
  length. References 12, 14 and 15 no longer repeat their corpus programs' algorithms: 12 is one
  pass with a stack, O(n); 14 keeps a distance matrix and each cluster's nearest, O(n²); 15 applies
  an edit only to the cells that depend on it, by change in value. On a count of clusters near -1e24, 14
  gives an error, where the earlier version panicked.
  Step rows and notes above that name a `.py` file record what was built at the time.
- The reference evaluator computes integers in `i64` and widens to a big integer instead of
  overflowing; a number past 2^20 bits is its `Overflow` error (L1.17). It has no fuel unless
  a caller sets one (docs/thresholds.md 8), and no limit on nested calls: its frames are on the heap (T2-eval). A divergent program
  at run time therefore ends only when time or memory does: `w(positional f) = f(f)` runs
  forever in constant space, and `w(positional f) = 1 + f(f)` grows until an allocation is
  refused (message, status 134) or the system kills it (no message). The operations on a
  `Value` keep their depth on the heap as well (K22); reading a variable still copies its
  `Value` (K21, T14-value).
- Coverage runs in CI (`cargo llvm-cov`, job `coverage`), not locally: this machine has no
  LLVM tools, and installing them is a system package change.
- Workspace lints: `missing_docs` warns, `unsafe_code` is forbidden. `zed-native` denies it
  instead and allows it at the two places that call and free JIT code; `zed-rt` needs none.

- No step waits for a person (the author's instruction, 2026-10-29; spec commit 827385b).
  M0(d) is now a prediction suite kept as tests, the M0(e) postmortems run alongside and gate
  nothing, and the corpus programs are corrected to fit the language rather than the reverse.
  When the spec is unclear, I choose, record the choice in DESIGN.md and here, and continue.

- `@exact` (docs/thresholds.md, replacement 8a): an opt-in for the member-by-member answer
  on ranges, never listed. An exact scope keeps the algebraic bounds and the written
  constraints, and is bottom exactly when no point of the bounded integer names meets them:
  each group of constraints sharing names is searched for one point (`preimage::witness`,
  branch and prune after Granger's class arithmetic), and the point is kept and checked
  again before any new search. A question about the exact set is a test assumed in the scope.
  No size limit, by default or otherwise (a default would be a threshold). Off by default;
  the annotation's syntax lands with L15.
- Enumeration (docs/thresholds.md, replacement 8): only sets the source lists are
  enumerated, each evaluation admitted by `stage::ends` and run with no fuel; ranges are left
  to the interval, congruence and relation domains. The M0.10 harness's instances (integers
  `-8..=8`, nine floats, 4,096 bindings) are test fixtures in `zed_tests::instances`, not a
  rule of Zed; the rung 3 and rung 6 budgets, never read by the compiler, were deleted.
- M0.5 values (DESIGN.md M0.5): widening moves a bound to the next landmark (a literal
  k as k − 1, k, k + 1) or to ±∞, at every head change, with no delay and no cap; narrowing
  moves a bound back to an old endpoint or a landmark and lets an infinite end take a bound
  once; phase 2 runs until a round changes nothing; a finite set widens to ⊤ at a member
  that is not a landmark (docs/thresholds.md, replacement 3); no constant bounds pieces or
  listings (3c): forward revision caps the smaller operand to ⌈(k + m)/k⌉ pieces and each
  sign region of the image to the operands' largest region, `x mod c` lists its first and
  last periods and one piece between, and the reduction lists an interval only at two
  members a piece; phase 1 rises, phase 2 and the reduction fall, asserted in test builds; Presburger relations
  have no size limit (replacement 4). Rule 1 of sec:constraints now says phase 1 is Bourdoncle's recursive
  strategy and only phase 2 runs in rounds; the sec:domains example is the tested three-cell
  loop. `flat(elems, top:)` is defined there (bottom `#empty`).
- M0.6 (DESIGN.md M0.6): the scalar sums devices as if run in sequence, an upper bound on
  the running time; L24 may refine the estimate but must keep it monotone in the frontier's
  quantities. The frontier is per device, because the scalar is not monotone in plan totals
  (work moved to a slower device costs more).
- M0.6a (DESIGN.md M0.6a): the footprint step M0.6 summed is now the peak of the schedule;
  retained bytes count until the schedule ends (COMPLEXITY.md C27), since `Region` carries no
  last reader. L3.23 and L24.5 fill `retained`. Since FOOTPRINT-overlap the plan records its
  schedule, and regions that run at once count together: exact under a static schedule, an
  upper bound under work stealing (COMPLEXITY.md C53). L3.23 and L24.5 fill `schedule`.
- M0.7 (DESIGN.md M0.7): the canonicalizer runs over kernel terms now and moves onto ZIR at
  L1.32. A canonical binder name is NUL then its level, which no source name can contain. The
  definition's own name, port names, atom names and catalog witnesses are part of the
  interface and so of the address. Renaming one binder per pass is O(n²) in the binders;
  L1.32 may do it in one pass if it gives the same normal form.
- M0.11 (DESIGN.md M0.11): an axiom is per arrow; a law every arrow of a name must have is
  listed at each kernel carrier. `+` at `f64` has identity -0.0, not 0.0. `min` and `max` at `int`
  have no identity. A unit has no version number: its address covers its exported
  declarations only, so its path and unused local declarations do not change it. The
  reference evaluator sets no memory limit; a step is a call, a `fix` round or a `gen` step.
  `DEFAULT_FUEL` was removed (docs/thresholds.md, replacement 8); the evaluator has no fuel
  unless a caller sets one. AXIOMS-order: a law relating two predicates is `Implies(q)` or
  `Composes(q, r)`, keyed by the first operator, so L3.8 finds the composition of links
  `a op b` and `b q c` as the axiom of `op` with law `Composes(q, _)`; transitivity stays
  `Transitive`, not `Composes(op, op)`. AXIOMS-gaps: `!=` at `f64` is only `Symmetric`
  (`NaN != NaN`), as DESIGN M0.11 says since c4f4680; `String` order is by code point, which
  `str::cmp` gives as UTF-8 byte order. AXIOMS-bool: `==` and `!=` at `bool` have the laws
  of `int` and `String`, as DESIGN M0.11 gives them at every carrier but `f64`. AXIOMS-chain-string:
  the order chain compositions hold at `String` as at `int`, keyed the same way. BIT-axioms:
  the bit words have no width, so their laws do not wrap; `shr` is floor division, and the
  harness checks the word operators by table on every width 1 to 8 rather than on rung 6.
  FLOAT-minmax: `min` and `max` at `f64` are IEEE 754-2019 `minimum` and `maximum` (DESIGN.md
  sec:reduction item 5), so they are selective, have identity `inf` and `-inf`, and have the NaN
  as zero; the harness compares `f64` constants by their bits.
- L1.1 (DESIGN.md sec:lexical): a leading byte order mark is rejected, like a file not in NFC;
  a lone `\r` is a line break. A U+FEFF after the start is the lexer's to reject. Dependency:
  `unicode-normalization`.
- L1.2 (DESIGN.md sec:lexical): a name is ASCII (NAME-ascii-only, 2026-11-12, which replaced
  the one-script rule); a word beyond ASCII is rejected with an offered ASCII name.
  Dependencies: `any_ascii`, `unicode-normalization`, `unicode-script`, `unicode-security`.
- L1.3: an integer token keeps its base and digits, not a value; `0755` is decimal, as the
  grammar reads it.
- L1.4: a float or rational token keeps its decimal text, not a value, so `1e400` lexes and its
  range is checked where its type is known; `0x10r` is rejected because `Rational` takes only
  decimal digits.
- L1.5: `"""` stripping applies only when both delimiters are on their own lines (DESIGN,
  sec:lexical, string row); a `"` string has no line break, its holes included, and a `//`
  comment in such a hole is its own error. An empty string is `Str([])`.
- L1.6: doc comments are kept outside the token stream, since the grammar discards every
  comment; the parser attaches them by span.
- L1.7: a fence's `// layer Lk` label may be on any whole comment line, since a fence's first
  line is usually its `// [d4]` header; the spec's `layer.label_of` reads only a program's first
  line, which gave EXAMPLES.md:432 layer L1 under its `// layer L2`. `sync.py` reads every line.
- L1.7: where a variant replaces a line instead of adding one (the loop variants of the fence
  at DESIGN.md:2420, a second `q =` or `rows =`), its fixture replaces that line, so the fixture has one
  error. The two column variants of the `orders` store edit its field type and put the ✗ there.
- VARIANT-sync: the fence at DESIGN.md:3303 (the `Counter` loop) says each variant replaces its
  `prev = c*.bump(3);` line, but its next line `until prev > 20;` reads `prev`, which the
  variants `c.bump(3);` and `_ = c*.bump(1); _ = c*.bump(2);` do not bind. Their fixtures
  write `until c.n > 20;` there, a change `fences::CHANGES` names; the fence itself could
  write `until c.n > 20;` (a spec edit, not made here). The two `orders` column variants make
  the `orders` line live with the ✗ and keep the commented line, also named there.
- L1.7: `…` is the name `…` (sec:grammar, "Documentation notation"); Part G said "a hole, not a
  token", now aligned to sec:grammar in DESIGN.md.
- TEST-fence-lines: a fence's section is the nearest heading above it with a `(sec:…)` label,
  not the nearest heading of any kind, so a fence under an unlabeled `###` of DESIGN.md (the
  remap law's "The legal moves") counts in its labeled section; EXAMPLES.md has no labels, so
  there the heading's text names the section. Two sections of one name count on from each other,
  so every key is distinct (`every_fence_key_is_its_own`).
- L1.8: the parser runs the copied grammar instead of a hand-written precedence climber, so
  its trees are `check.py`'s by construction and the grammar cannot drift from the spec
  unnoticed (DESIGN.md L1.8 now says so). It parses every form of every layer at L1; steps
  L1.9–L1.12 add the elaboration of their forms, and the elaborator rejects a node whose
  alternative's layer (`Tree::layer`) is above the program's.
- L1.8: a variant of a documentation-notation fence is parsed as a `DocFence`, as its fence
  is (`exec : … -> Rows | #sqlError` is a signature without its `;`).
- L1.9: the expression syntax tree is built from the parse tree after parsing, not by the
  parser, which only records rule, alternative and tokens. Each later step adds its forms to
  `zedc::ast`, and the fence test's counts of built and later chains move with them. `^` is
  built here with the other operators of the L1.8 ladder, ahead of its L1.10 listing. The
  uniform call stays a call of a member until resolution (L1.14, L1.16).
- L1.10: the type expressions are built here, ahead of their L1.12 listing, since `is T` and a
  lambda's `x: T` are written with them; L1.12 still adds the declarations that use them. A
  destructuring parameter `((s, c)) -> …` and patterns other than atom patterns are L2.
- L1.11: a block in expression position must export; a declaration's body block need not
  (`Counter.tick() { n' = n + 1; }`), and L1.12 builds those. Statement order has no
  meaning, so a `return` may precede a binding. A name bound twice in one block is left to
  name resolution (L1.14).
- L1.12: a unit's top level holds declarations and pushes, not an export, so `return` there
  is an error. A function's several `test` tables are one list of cases in written order.
  The result form `f(x) -> T = …` is L10 by the grammar and is not built at L1.
- L1.13: the formatter's layout is not given in full by DESIGN.md, so these choices are
  recorded there: two-space indentation; no line breaking by width (a known limit, revisit
  when the corpus has long lines); a block on one line only when it holds just a one-line
  export and no comment; a function body always on several lines; several `test` tables
  joined into one; a comment inside a statement but outside its blocks moved to the end of
  the statement. A block that is an operand opens with a statement at L1, so its export is
  written `return e;`. The builder stores a block's export last, so "the same AST" holds
  exactly.
- L1.14: where DESIGN.md is silent, recorded there: a function's or lambda's parameters and
  output ports share one scope with its body block's statements; a parameter's type and
  default see the parameters but not the body; `test` cases are read around the function;
  an `else` pattern's `f:` fields are in scope in its default only; functions of one name
  whose written parameter types differ form an overload set; a member `x.f` is recorded only
  when `f` is bound in the unit (fields are told apart at L1.16); the L1 prelude words are the
  numeric casts and `abs`, `len`, `lower`, `upper`, `trim`, `sum` (`count` takes a family, so
  L3); the L1 type names are `int`, `rat`, `f64`, `bool`, `String`, `Lines`, `Files`.
- L1.15: the kernel already had all seven generators (M0.9); "whole" adds the `ev` of
  `fold(F, op, ev)` and `fix(F0, step, ev)`. The record maps a property name to a grade; a
  property absent is Unknown, and a derived property is stored at the meet of its premises'
  grades (the rule and premises are the property tracker's), so the tags are Axiom,
  CheckedExhaustive, Proved, Bounded, Obligated, Assumed, and only the first three are proof
  grade. The record is part of the term, so it is serialized into the address, and VERSION is
  now 2. The printer's notation: binary primitives infix and always parenthesized, other
  primitives as functions, a generator's named parts as `depth: 2`, `witness: residue`,
  `join: union`, `guard: before`, `definedness`, the record as `ev: { associative: axiom }`;
  ports as `port.read(stdin)` and `port.push(stdout, e)`. A term that does not fit puts each
  part of its outermost list on its own line, two spaces in, and an `if` breaks both branches
  together.
- L1.16: `++` is its own kernel primitive `Concat`, not `Add`, since `+` and `++` are distinct
  operators with different laws (DESIGN.md, Property tracking); `^` is `Pow`. Every binder
  gets a kernel name unique in the unit: its own name, or `name@k` when another binder shares
  the name or the name is a prelude word (so the word stays a free variable for the
  interpreter, L1.18); temporaries are `$k`. Because names are unique, a default is filled by
  let-binding the call's arguments under the parameters' names and then the defaults in their
  own dependency order, with no capture. Statements of a scope are ordered by their uses; a
  cycle, self-reference included, is an error that names layer L6 (recursion). `e else d` and
  `x?.f` match any atom (`AnyAtom`, `#_`), exact while atoms are loose (before L2). A call
  through a value (lambda, prelude word) passes arguments by position only; named arguments
  there wait for types (L1.26). `test` tables belong to top-level functions; a key is the
  argument, or the tuple of all arguments in declaration order. Deferred as errors: rationals,
  integers beyond 64 bits and named atom payloads (L1.17), `is` (L1.22), lambda defaults
  (L1.26), overloads and fields (L2).
  Self-reference resolves to itself; cycles are a later step's.
- L1.17: the spec said both IEEE `==` (sec:type_resolution) and "`==` reflexive at f64, bitwise"
  (M0.11); IEEE wins for the language's `==` and the comparisons, and bitwise identity stays
  for keys and law checks (Rust `Eq` on `Value`). M0.11 and the axioms are corrected. `==`
  compares atoms instead of passing them through, since it has an arrow at every type; the
  m0.10 helpers that used `x == x` to pass a failure now match `#_`. Comparing numbers of two
  kinds, or `1r + 1`, is a type error; `1 == 1.0` is false. A payload is all by position or
  all by name; field order is not part of the value. `==` on functions is a type error naming
  L1.22. The size limit of 2^20 bits, and the elaboration error of a rat literal past it, were
  removed by CAP-bits: numbers have no size limit.
- L1.18: several failing operands now merge into `#errs` of the set of them, replacing M0.9's
  "leftmost atom wins" (DESIGN.md M0.9 (a) is corrected), so `#a + #b` and `#b + #a` agree.
  The set is a family mapping each failure to itself. Origin sets wait for origin tokens
  (L1.20). Cast grammars: `int` reads `-?digits`; `rat` reads `3r`, `-1r/3r`, `2/4` or
  `0.25`; `f64` reads `-?` then `inf`, `nan` or `digits[.digits][e-?digits]`, and a finite
  text past the float range is `#inexact`. `+5`, `.5` and `infinity` are `#invalid`.
  `upper` uses full case mapping (`"straße"` to `"STRASSE"`). Fixed notation up to 10^21
  means `1e16` prints as `10000000000000000.0`.
- L1.19: read failures are the bare `#ioError` the types write (`Files = Path ->? String |
  #ioError`, `LineNo -> String | #ioError`), since payload patterns arrive at L2; only the
  write acknowledgment carries `#ioError(why)`, and the program never sees it. A port pushed
  twice is caught at run time, not statically, because two push sites on two branches are
  legal. Elaboration turns `v[k]` into `tupleGet` for a literal key and an application
  otherwise, so until L1.22 the evaluator reads a family or a lookup port either way.
  Files are written through `Lines` ports bound to paths (`out=path`); a `Files` output
  waits for families (L3).
- L1.20: a non-recursive call is named by its call site in the static half of the address
  (the spec's list of region instances leaves calls out); recursion is keyed by entry key
  at L6. A region's operator calls are aimed at the operand's position, so two operators of
  one region differ though their keypaths match. A primitive a region calls is no fact.
  Recording is opt-in and does not change the value; retention policy arrives with
  sec:security's lineage sampling.
- L1.21: the spec left the program test form to this step; it is a table on `main` (a
  `Files` port given as a lambda, since a family display is L3) and the `// ✗` marks, the
  convention the documentation's fences already use. Only the first rejecting phase reports,
  so marks in a later phase go unchecked; an aborting wave fails its row. The spec's command
  is `zed test`; the binary is `zedc`, as for `run`.
- L1.22: the tuple and morphism parts are not reduced to a canonical form, so equal sets can
  print differently; type equality is subtyping both ways (L1.23). `is` can tell a function
  from other values and nothing finer until families carry their types (L3). A keypath is a
  tuple, a family a morphism; `() -> V` is keyed by the empty tuple; `->?` is partial at
  each level. `Lines` and `Files` are port types only.
- L1.23: a clause of morphism types is decided one negated type at a time, so it is sound
  and incomplete when several negated types together cover the positive part. A value type
  with a parameter under a complement or right of `\` counts as possibly empty (monotonicity).
  All members of a group take the same parameters. Tuple components that mention the group
  stay lazy nodes, so building a recursive type never unfolds it. The memo is per thread and
  never cleared. `Env` and its members form a reference cycle that leaks, once per instance.
  Recursive types are kernel `Group`s here; `type` declarations map onto them at L2.
- L1.24: the spec's "symbolic affine bounds" are given a numeric floor, since the join of
  `[0]` and `[1..=n]` is `[0..=max(0, n)]` and not `[0..=n]`; without it every counting loop
  loses its bound. Ends stay 64-bit and saturate outward. A symbol is named by its source text
  and its range is not known to the domain (so `a::len >= 0` is not used); the reduction with
  the other domains, which would supply it, is L1.39. Bounds with different terms are not
  compared, so `int[0..=n]` and `int[0..=n + m]` are both kept by a meet. The finite-set domain
  holds kernel values; strings' lengths are counted in characters (code points after NFC).
- L1.25: a preimage is a box; a relation among inputs is projected and marked necessary until
  L1.38. `x * x <= 99` reaches `[-9..=9]` through the power reading, exact, rather than by the
  enumeration the plan names. Because `==` and `!=` compare failures as data, a comparison whose
  operands may fail keeps its box unless the other side is a constant integer; the kernel's own
  `&&` and `||` pass failures through, so their union is exact only when neither side can fail
  (the surface `&&` elaborates to a branch). There is no hash primitive in the kernel, so the
  stops are string operations, foreign names and terms outside the scalar catalog. Congruences
  for `mod` over unbounded operands are L1.39.
- L1.26: an undeclared parameter is a class of a union-find forest (`check::Class`): the
  carriers its values may take, and whether other values. Uses narrow and merge classes; the
  body is checked once; a class left with several carriers gives a bounded variable (`area(w,
  h) = w * h` is `(w: T, h: T) -> T for T in int | f64 | rat`), and one holding a literal the
  first of int, f64 and rat, since a body elaborates once, so `f(x) = x * 2` is `(x: int) ->
  int`. A nested function reads the outer classes, so its signature may name the outer
  function's variable. A use that would empty a class is the error, at that use. No derived
  variables: an operator's result over a class is the class and the atoms of every arrow
  still possible. A float literal never adopts int. A type variable used as a tuple or a function
  gives `_` (`first(p) = p[0]` is `(p: T) -> _`). Atoms pass through operators but not into
  declared functions or lambdas. A divisor whose type holds no zero adds no `#divByZero`. The
  first arrow that fits a combination gives its result. An application over unions keeps one
  state per set of arrows still alive, with no cap.
- L1.26a: a literal is generic only as an operand of a binary operator other than `==` and
  `!=`; as a call argument (`f(x, 1n)`), a tuple component, a bound, a recursive call or at a
  declared type `kn` reads as `k`, since only the operator gives it another operand to follow.
  The body is not specialized per carrier: the `match` that picks `T(k)` runs once per
  evaluation, and folds only when the stager evaluates a whole call at build stage. The new
  step unit moved the parity split of `l01_29_diagnostics::stable`, whose smaller piece fell
  to 20 runs, so its floor `FEWEST` is 10 (was 20).
- L1.27: L1 has no `type` declaration, so every atom an L1 program meets is loose, and
  run-time `else` defaults every atom; step L2.5 must set the family marking from `type`, and
  step L2.4 make elaboration keep the atoms the checker protected (an arm before `#_`). A pattern with a
  payload keeps its atom in the type.
- L1.28: a local binding counts as demanded when its body names it, even in a branch cut
  later. `Program::stage` is not yet used by the `zed` command; the residual program is used
  by lowering (L1.33). The `left` entries of `stage::Report` carry the term and the stop;
  L1.29 turns them into derivations (DESIGN.md sec:diagnostics now requires every rejection
  to show the full derivation: each constraint, its site, and the path it took).
- L1.29: no ✗ variant in `zed/fences/variants` reaches its documented error at L1: four
  stop at an L2 declaration, three fail to parse at L1, two use `…`, and the two that pass
  the mark check pass for other reasons (`Point` undefined; a parse error on the marked line). The test pins what
  each gives; the step that enables a variant must change its pin to the documented error.
  The staging report (`stage::Report.left`) is not a rejection and gives each left term its
  reason without a derivation. A first exclusion of "stale" search records cut the chain of
  a top-level value read in a searched body; it was removed, since every run re-records each
  subexpression before deriving any error in it. A step of a block derives no further than
  the block (its export is not followed yet), and a literal binding shows as "this
  expression is 4" rather than as a literal. A derivation is not cut: each expression in
  it is derived once (docs/thresholds.md, replacement 2), so it is at most the size of the
  program.
- L1.30: keys are syntactic (the `Debug` print of kernel terms), so an alpha-renaming or a
  renumbered `name@k` binder reruns a row that a canonical key would reuse. Kernel names are
  numbered per source name in binder order, so adding a same-named binder before another
  renames it and reruns the rows that reach it. Results are never evicted. `zedc run`
  compiles its one unit once, so it calls `run::compile` directly. Found on the way:
  `zedc test` printed a rejection's message without its derivation; fixed.
- L1.31 (DESIGN.md L1.31): regions are isolated; a value from outside enters as a capture,
  an input after the node's fixed ones received as a trailing argument. State edges are linear
  and enter only match and port regions. A certificate region holds only kernel nodes. The
  validator checks structure only; edge-type fit is the checker's, for the term lowered from.
  The text form starts `zir 1`, one line per header, node and results, keyed by path, read
  back in any order; a literal pattern is `=v`; a recursive type has no text form until L2.
  The binary form starts `ZIR\0` and the version, stores edges as their text, floats by their
  bits. Errors give line and column, or byte offset.
- L1.32 (DESIGN.md L1.32): on ZIR the binder rule renames match-pattern binders to their
  index in the pattern, the written name a hint on the argument edge; the other rules run per
  value edge in preorder. The address hashes `zed-zir\0`, the M0.7 version and the binary
  form of the normal form (a level name begins with NUL, which the text form cannot read).
- The two zeros (DESIGN sec:type_resolution, "Equality and order corner rules"): `==` and the orders read `0.0 == -0.0`, and a tuple compares component by component in IEEE order (`Value::surface_cmp`); key formation and lookup turn `-0.0` into `0.0` at any depth (`Value::key`), which the kernel had not done before. Identity keeps them apart: kernel `Eq` on values, laws, and the content address, which hashes a float by its bits and every NaN as `0x7ff8000000000000`. Tests: `m0_11_prelude_axioms_and_limits/signed_zero.rs` and the kernel test `the_two_zeros_are_one_key`.
- L1.33 (DESIGN.md L1.33): a primitive used as a value lowers to a `prim` node with no
  inputs, not to a lambda, since the kernel tells them apart; a variadic primitive has no such
  form. Captures and state edges are taken on demand; a function that uses a port is inlined
  at each call. CSE keys a node by the address of a one-node region; a node with a state input
  never repeats one, so effects are never merged. Edges carry `_` until code generation.
- L1.34 (DESIGN.md L1.34): a constant is static and never counted; integers, floats, booleans,
  the empty tuple and bare atoms are unboxed. A call to a callee the plan cannot see passes
  owned. Loop and family regions run in the kernel, which borrows their inputs; a family's
  entries are kernel data until L3.17. Scalar, family and port nodes take their value from the
  kernel, which runs each node alone; tuples, closures, calls, branches and matches run in the
  checking machine, so it keeps the program's sharing.
- L1.35 (DESIGN.md L1.35): MLIR is reached through its text form and `mlir-opt`/`mlir-translate`,
  so no C++ build enters the tree; the C API is adopted only if compile time measured at L28
  shows the process boundary matters. MLIR's bufferization and ownership-based deallocation
  are not used for Zed values; the L1.34 plan is applied before the lowering.
- T3 (Z8, Z9, Z9b): a node holds its region and index, not a copy, and paths exist only in
  messages. The `if` releases an owned condition the arms do not take at the test, on the
  path where it is not a boolean, which saves an `rt_dec` per `if`; counts equal the
  machine's. `docs/wip/z8-z9-stopped.patch` stays, for the author to delete; this
  `early` release was the one part of it not yet landed. One function's frame is linear
  in its words, so a term thousands deep needs a stack of megabytes at run time. Sharing
  slots between sibling arms would reduce that.
- L1.36 (DESIGN.md L1.36): a value is a word of a tag and a payload, returned in two
  registers. Arms are inline; a lambda body is a function, with an entry function taking every
  argument owned for calls the plan cannot resolve. Nodes outside the inline tier are run by
  the runtime through the kernel, so the native and machine counts agree one for one; the
  runtime's state is thread-local, and a hook never calls generated code. A match that native
  pattern matching does not decide is decided by the kernel, and the two must agree. The
  object file is checked for reproducibility and its symbols; linking it into an executable
  comes with step L1.36a. The workspace's `unsafe_code` lint is relaxed only in `zed-native`.
- L1.36a (DESIGN.md L1.36a): an executable carries the graph, not the tables, and plans it
  again at its start, since `Tables::new` numbers nodes as the code generator did; the code
  passes node numbers and the hooks read the tables by them. The runtime library is the whole
  `zed-native` crate as a static library (114 MB), and `-Wl,--gc-sections` keeps the part an
  executable reaches (14 MB). Cargo copies `libzed_native.a` beside `zedc` only in a build of
  `zed-native` itself; a test build leaves it as `deps/libzed_native-HASH.a`, so the tests name
  the one built with them (NATIVE-lib-pick, NATIVE-build-id: `link::runtime_of` matches the bytes of the section
  `.zed_native.build`, `link::BUILD`: a type's `TypeId`, which covers the crate's hash, and a
  hash of `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` from `build.rs`; a stripped `zedc` keeps the section, not
  its symbols, and the crate's hash leaves the compiler flags out; the newest by time
  was wrong when three variants sat in `deps`). `zedc build` refuses, with status 2, a runtime
  library from another build than its own: `cargo test -p zed-native` with other features
  rewrites `zedc` but not the `libzed_native.a` beside it (seen 2026-11-05). The system libraries are those `rustc --print native-static-libs` gives
  on x86-64 Linux with glibc; another host is PORTABLE-rt. A link is about 1.5 s at load 60.
  Usage words of an executable name it by its `argv[0]`.
- L1.36b (DESIGN.md L1.36b): the key of a link is a BLAKE3 hash (`link::Identity::key`,
  derived key "zed-native 2026-11-07 the key of a link") over, each after its length: the
  object file's bytes; the BLAKE3 hash of the runtime library's bytes; what the driver writes
  for `--version` and for `-Wl,--version`; the system libraries and `-Wl,--gc-sections`.
  `zedc build` passes it to the linker as `-Wl,--build-id=0x...`, so the executable records
  it, and `link::recorded` reads it back (`object`'s `build_id`); an output that records the
  key it would link with is left as it is, and `--report`'s link row counts it cached. Why
  each: the object file holds the program and the code generator's output, so its bytes cover
  both; the runtime library by its bytes, not by its `.zed_native.build` section, since that
  section does not change with the crate's source (checked 2026-11-07: a function added to
  `link.rs`, `zedc` rebuilt, the section's bytes the same), so a library left from older
  source passes L1.36a's check (proposed follow-up: `build.rs` hashes the crate's sources
  into `BUILD`); the linker by its driver's reports, two spawns under 5 ms, which name the
  driver's release and through it the linker's, and do not depend on the path (gcc writes its
  `argv[0]` file name, so `cc` and `gcc` give two keys; clang writes its `InstalledDir`).
  Hashing the 117 MB library costs about 0.1 s per build; a kept build of a small program
  took 0.05 s against 0.74 s for a link. A driver that fails or writes nothing for either
  version is refused, status 1, each with its own message; a missing one is status 2. Not in
  the key: the system libraries' and C start files' bytes and the driver's environment
  (`LIBRARY_PATH`, `COMPILER_PATH`), so a system update under one driver release is not seen
  (proposed: read the inputs ld lists with `--dependency-file` and hash them); a stripped or
  edited output keeps the build ID and is kept. Both fixed by LINK-key-deps (below). Collision resistance of BLAKE3 is an
  assumption of the trusted base, as for content addresses. Found while testing: a build
  killed between writing `out.zed.o` and removing it leaves the file, and every later build
  to `out` fails with "File exists" until it is deleted (L1.36a's `create_new`; proposed:
  give the message that names the file to delete, or write the object under a fresh name).
  Fixed by LINK-obj-leftover (below).
- LINK-obj-leftover (after L1.36b): a build that links works in a directory of its own beside
  `out`, `<out>.zed-build.<pid>.<k>` (`link::Scratch`), held locked with `flock` while the build
  lives; the object file is written there, the linker writes the executable there, and a
  rename moves it to `out`, so a build reading `out` at the same time (for its key, or to run
  it) sees a whole executable, before or after. The directory is removed on success, on error
  and in unwinding from a panic (`Drop`). SIGKILL or SIGINT leave it; the kernel releases the
  lock when the process ends, and the next build of `out` that links removes every such
  directory whose lock it can take (`link::sweep`), never one a running build holds; after
  its lock a name must still name the directory locked, so a sweep that removes a directory
  just made and not yet locked makes that build take another name. A file at the old name
  `<out>.zed.o` is neither read nor removed. A kept build (equal key) reads and writes
  nothing beside `out`. Changes: `out` is replaced by rename, so a symbolic link at `out` is
  replaced by the executable and its target is left as it was (ld wrote through it before);
  `out` naming no file (`dir/..`) is status 2 with its own message.
- RUNTIME-build-src (after L1.36b): the build in `.zed_native.build` now ends with the BLAKE3
  hash of the sources of zed-native and of the workspace crates it depends on
  (`zed_native::sources`, written by `build.rs`). It reads more than the compiler does: a file
  under `src` that no module names, and a file a `#[cfg(test)]` module names by `#[path]`
  (`tests/src/scaling.rs`, in zedc and zed-kernel), change it. That costs only a needless
  rebuild; leaving out a file the compiler reads would let a stale runtime pass. A path built
  by a macro is not followed; the only ones are under `OUT_DIR`, made by a build script that
  is itself hashed.
- LINK-key-deps (after L1.36b): the key of a link names every file the linker read, by its
  bytes, and the driver's environment. The link passes `-Xlinker --dependency-file=<scratch>`
  (`-Wl,` would split the path at commas); the list is read in both forms measured here, GNU
  ld 2.46 (two-space indent, no escapes) and LLD 22 (one space, `\ `, `\#`, `$$` escaped),
  a path taken as written when it names a file and unescaped otherwise (`link::dependencies`).
  `link::Inputs::of` hashes each distinct file once, by (device, inode), and skips the object
  file and the runtime library, already in the key. The environment variables are
  `link::DRIVER_ENV`; PATH is left out, since the driver's and linker's versions stand for
  what it finds. The build ID is written twice: the link writes the key without the inputs,
  and `write_build_id` replaces those 32 bytes of the note's descriptor with the full key.
  Then the executable is hashed and the record `<out>.zed-link` written (`zed-link 1`, the
  hash in hex, the paths each ended by a zero byte); `out` is renamed first and the record
  after, so a record never describes bytes that are not at `out`. Why a record and not a
  second note: the executable cannot hold the hash of its own bytes. A kept build re-reads
  each recorded file (O(total input bytes), about the cost of the runtime's hash) and the
  output. Refusals, status 1, each with its own message: a linker that writes no list; a
  listed file that cannot be read now; an output without the build ID it was given. Limit,
  as for any cache built on dependency lists: a new file that appears earlier on a search
  path, while no file the last link read changed, is not seen; so is a change to
  `/etc/ld.so.conf` alone, which GNU ld reads only for a needed library found in no directory
  before it (a `zedc build` link opened it zero times under strace; the library found is
  listed and hashed). `GNUTARGET` added after the orchestrator's check of the ld man page.
  Found while testing: helper
  files in the working directory had fixed names (`program.o`), which an output of that name
  met; they are now named after the output.
- L1.37 (DESIGN.md L1.37): the checker records each top-level `=` binding's type, and
  `elab::Def::first_order` says whether it has no function component. A binding typed `_`, as
  a higher-order call's result is at L1, is compared too, since both engines refuse a function
  result with the same error. Outcomes are compared as text: the printed value or the error,
  and for a wave each port's bytes. A `Files` port in the harness holds the input text at every
  path. `oracle::ENABLED` is the enabled layer and rises with each layer; the corpus joins at
  L3. The reorder-facet rule (a float compared by its type and keys) is due at L9.
  Since ORACLE-chain the bindings run together, as one tuple, and each is still given what a
  run of it alone gives (its value, or the error of the first stop its run reaches); `Runs`
  finds those outcomes where the tuple cannot be run.
- L1.38 (DESIGN.md L1.38): since T4 the solver's integers are unbounded (`store::int`, i128 while a value fits), so no coefficient refuses a question.
  Replacement 4 removed `VARIABLES`, `ATOMS`, `INTERMEDIATE` and `KEPT_CONJUNCTIONS`: the
  Omega test eliminates a variable only while the rows stay within the input's count, decides
  an inexact step by the real and dark shadows or leaves it undecided (`Entailment::Undecided`),
  and does not split a formula into its conjunctions: disjuncts are pruned against the base,
  a point is sought greedily with one level of lookahead, and a projection meets the unions of
  each disjunct's projections; a scope projects a part of its relation again only when its
  names' intervals or congruences changed (docs/thresholds.md §4, COMPLEXITY.md S16); a product atom's countermodel is checked against the real product, and a
  point where it fails is "not proved". `Preimage::relation` is kept only on a result that is
  not exact. The congruence `x mod 7 != 3` over a range is kept as a relation, necessary
  (enumeration of ranges was removed by docs/thresholds.md, replacement 8).
- L1.38, T4 (cross-check XV Q9): `presburger::decide` answers whether a conjunction has an integer
  point without building one. A system is split into parts that share no variable; a part of
  two variables is decided exactly (`twovar`), one whose rows are all of two unit terms by the
  zero-weight cycle parity test (`utvpi`), and the rest by the Omega test with dark and gray
  shadows. Splinters are split again while each dark elimination of one leaves fewer live variables
  than the one it came from (OMEGA-splinter-cap); a point that could lie only in a splinter split
  again with as many live variables is refused (`Refusal::Shadows`); the elimination that would
  enlarge the rows is refused (`Refusal::Growth`) as DESIGN L1.38 records. The simplex is only a
  proof that a system has no rational point, and gives the last step a vertex to try. Dantzig's
  rule and Bland's rule decide the same feasibility, but the vertex differs, so the rule can
  change a Growth refusal into a point: with Bland's rule from the first pivot, a unit
  three-term family at 16 variables went from a point to Growth. The checker asks, for each
  function other than `main` whose body the linear-relation domain states, whether the body can
  hold and whether it can fail (`run::linear_questions`); a refusal is a rejection with its
  cause, the function's span and the constraints, and a decided question rejects nothing. The
  parameters' types are not read there, so the domains are unbounded, and a question typed
  bounds would decide can be refused. Of 400 dense four-variable systems with coefficients up
  to 7, about 150 are refused with Growth. A refused dark shadow is the answer: its splinters
  are not searched, since they could only turn the refusal into a point, and searching them
  ran the test again once per lower bound of each dark elimination (a chain into a refused
  block, 64 to 512 variables: 33.5 times the work before, about 11 after; the oracle's 400
  four-variable answers did not change). The simplex switches to Bland's rule for good after 4
  to 12 pivots on the `tight` probe family, so in practice it is Bland's rule; a rule that
  returns to Dantzig's at each new least total violation was tried and measured worse (shifted
  sparse family 26.9 times the work from 128 to 1,024, over the limit of 24; `tight` at 64
  variables 46 s against 9 s), and was not kept.

  elimination, the side with fewer bounds (Pugh's lemma holds for `-x` too), and the first
  refused splinter is the answer, so a later splinter that has a point is not reached: a
  judgment taken here for linear work, which left the oracle's 400 answers unchanged. Pugh's
