- L1.38, LIVE3 (author decision 2026-11-03: a linear program in a fixed dimension is allowed at three live variables only): `store::live3` decides a part left with three variables, once no elimination keeps the rows, completely, so Growth and Shadows now need four variables or more. Method: Megiddo's prune-and-search for a linear program in dimension three (deterministic, by medians, no simplex and no random choice), in exact rationals with infinitesimals for ties; a simplex of points of the rows from six such programs, rounded with a fixed ratio (the rows lie within the simplex scaled by 25 about its centroid); an exact LLL reduction of that shape, giving Babai's point (tried against the rows) or a direction whose width over the rows is at most w(3), a constant of dimension three and not a size; each value along it is a plane, given two variables by a unimodular completion and decided by `twovar::point`. Entered from the box stage of `Omega::run` where the box decides nothing and `live == 3`, and from the splinter search, so a gray shadow over three variables is decided too. The answer is order-free because the method is complete; the point found may depend on order. `Int` got 64-bit fast paths in `div_floor`, `mod_floor` and `*` (about 10% fewer instructions in callgrind). Counts changed, each with its reason in the test's comment: the small-coefficient oracle (0x38_0a) 261, 3, 136 → 274, 4, 122; the corner oracle (0x38_3b) 2,611, 9,306, 83 → 2,631, 9,331, 38 (both measured after the rebase onto main with HULL3); refused systems in the three-term naming test 13 (bound lowered from more than 20 to more than 10); the checker's, `omega.rs`'s and the `l01_21` row test's Shadows examples moved to four variables (the three-variable ones are now decided); `s22::chains_of_slow_families` counts 6 boxes found exact by classes of remainders, was 7, since `mod7 k=2`, refused by Shadows in the transfer before, is now decided there with the same exact box, and the Growth message says four variables or more. The disjunct-order test is split into four quarters of the same 2,000 formulas (each asserts more than 250 of 500 reordered, together at least the old more than 1,000), since live3 made the whole take 42 s under load 58 (control 20 s): measured alone at load 60, 16.9, 13.8, 10.8 and 18.4 s. New tests in `l01_38_presburger::live3`: random bounded and unbounded systems, flat systems and equalities, rationally empty systems, Reeve tetrahedra under unimodular maps, all against enumeration; corner cases; order independence; the Omega test on three variables. Scaling, n and 8n in instructions (repair 1, after the verifier found that the first rows family was decided by the first linear program, so LLL and the planes were never measured): Reeve's tetrahedron of height 7 shrunk, with m rows that each hold the whole body with slack 0 to 5, so every stage runs (22 planes); rows 256 → 2,048, 8.18 times (1.92e9 → 1.57e10); bits 64 → 512 at 8 rows, 12.81 times at power 1 (both sizes past the i128 path of `Int`); the same body under a shear of B/2-bit entries, 10.28 times (probe). Negative controls, run once and not committed: an all-pairs `Lin2::minus` pass in each round of `solve2` fails the rows test at 33.1; an extra factor of B in `Q::mul` fails the bits test on bytes at 35.0 (instructions 21.7); an all-pairs pass of additions over the rows of each plane is not caught (10.2), since it is small next to `twovar`. Rebased onto main (HULL3 and the presburger.rs change): the `hull3` stage runs first where a unit side exists and `live3` at the box stage after it; HULL3 decides nothing LIVE3 does not (the oracle counts are those of LIVE3 alone), so it is subsumed in what it decides (ledger item HULL3-subsumed); which runs first is for that item to measure. `more_random_guarded_chains_keep_their_preimages` counts 55 made exact, was 56: the transfer before, which shares the solver, now decides by `live3` the gray shadow of one chain (`(if ((i mod 3) == 2) { … } < 6)`), so both are exact and alike there (shown by turning off the call of `live3` in splinters, which gives 56 again).
- L1.38, HULL3-subsumed (2026-11-05): the task was to keep `hull3::shadow` as a first try before
  `live3` if it is faster on the unit-side class, and otherwise to remove it. Removed. On
  `decide`, in instructions (load 47 to 57): the wide unit-side rows of `stages::three_rows`
  (coefficients up to a million, 3 seeds summed) at 64 / 512 / 4,096 rows took 261M / 3,705M /
  38,929M with the stage and 203M / 501M / 1,369M without it; the tangent lens over (5000,
  5000), where no box point holds, at 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 / 1,024 pairs took 355M / 894M /
  2,198M / 5,146M / 11,712M with it and 941M / 1,489M / 4,092M / 4,348M / 7,163M without it
  (processor time 47 / 117 / 306 / 676 / 1,547 ms against 146 / 225 / 620 / 660 / 1,143 ms;
  bytes 129M → 4,205M against 33.6M → 399M). The stage is faster on small lenses (at most 3.1
  times in processor time, 3.5 in wall time), slower from 1,024 pairs, 28 times slower on the
  wide rows, and grows 10 to 14 times per factor 8 where `live3` alone grows 2.5 to 4.8 times; it
  never ran on rows with coefficients up to 5 or on empty pairs of rows. Since the gain is at
  most a constant factor on one family and the loss grows with the size, it was removed rather
  than kept as a first try (a first try that sometimes loses a factor of 28 is not faster).
  Tests: every case of `hull3.rs` moved to `live3.rs` (random systems, coincident planes,
  planes through one line or one point, normals in one plane, unbounded and empty systems),
  checked against enumeration through `point`; `the_shadow_scales` became
  `a_lens_of_tangent_planes_away_from_the_origin_scales` on `decide` (128 → 1,024 pairs, 4.8
  times the instructions, 6.9 times the bytes), with `a_lens_of_tangent_planes_has_a_point`.
  Negative control, run once and not committed: all pairs of the bounds of the unit variable in
  place of the stage fail that test at 53.2 times the bytes (21.9M → 1,167M, load 45).
  `stages::three_variables_in_many_rows_scale` failed on bytes at 64 → 512 (26.0, limit 24):
  at 64 rows `live3` finds the point in 6.7M instructions, a path the larger sizes do not take
  (210M at 128), so its sizes are now 128 → 1,024 (1.9 times the instructions, 3.2 the bytes).
  Found: `live3::point` alone on the tangent lens over the origin grows irregularly (128 / 256
  / 512 / 1,024 pairs: 595M / 1,461M / 42,807M / 32,633M instructions; bytes 41.6 times from 128
  to 1,024), with 99.8% of the time in the linear programs (`simplex`, `solve2`, `side`,
  `solve1`, `least`, `on_line`, `eval1`: rational additions and gcds of large integers, by
  perf). `satisfiable` does not reach `point` on that lens, since a box point holds it. New
  ledger item LIVE3-lp-tangents; the test `a_lens_of_tangent_planes_scales_in_point` is
  ignored until it is fixed. Oracle counts unchanged: (274, 5, 121) and (2631, 9340, 29).
- L1.38, LIVE3-lp-tangents (2026-11-05): the growth reported by HULL3-subsumed is a change of path, not of cost. Counted at 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 / 1,024 pairs: 311M / 591M / 1,464M / 42,632M / 32,486M instructions. At 128 pairs the rounded vertex of the first linear program (direction e0) holds the rows, so `point` stops after it, on i128 numbers; at 512 it runs five linear programs and at 1,024 three, and the directions f2 and f3 have 12 to 23 digits, so the arithmetic moves to the heap (bytes 21.2M → 881.6M). The work of each linear program is linear (35k to 345k `solve1` pieces from 128 to 1,024), and the size of every number has a bound that does not depend on the row count. A different f3 is not possible: it is the normal of three vertices, unique up to sign, and the rounding argument needs it exact. The scaling test therefore uses a family that runs the whole of `point` at every size: the lens cut by 10^6 + 1/4 <= Z <= 10^6 + 1/2 (8 to 1,024 pairs: 223M / 1,420M / 1,238M / 3,598M / 6,373M / 14,878M / 29,056M / 112,080M instructions). The cause was found with counters added for the run (work, evaluations, linear programs, time per linear program), not with perf.
- L1.38, RUNG2-mod-symbol (2026-11-05): rung 2 reads `a div n` and `a mod n` for a divisor `n`
  that is not a constant. The definition is a disjunction over the sign of `n`, so a premise
  that fixes the sign leaves one disjunct; at `n == 0`, where the operation fails, the quotient
  and remainder are free, so from `n >= 0` neither `0 <= x mod n < n` nor `x div n * n + x mod
  n == x` is proved (the answer is "not proved", since a point that gives `n * q0` a value that
  is no product is no countermodel). `a div n` and `a mod n` share one pair, looked up by
  dividend and divisor; without that, `x div n * n + x mod n == x` was not proved even from
  `n >= 1`. Two relations still number their pairs apart, so a premise and a goal that both
  name `x mod n` get two pairs and nothing links them: a fact that needs them equal is not
  proved. `presburger::products` takes the products it wants from relation bodies only, not
  from definitions, as before.
- L1.38, RUNG2-carrier (2026-11-08): `front::linear_questions` skips a function when any parameter is not int-only, not just that parameter, because `Scoped::relation` takes one input per parameter (a debug assertion). So a function over `x: int, y: f64` gets no rung 2 question even on its `x` part; the test driver, which calls `relations` directly, reads such a part. A generic, literal-free function (`ok(a, b) = a < b`) is generic over `int | f64 | rat`, so it is no longer asked: the growth rows of `checker.rs` without their literals were refused on main and now pass. The ASSOC-infer study is untouched.
- L1.38, RUNG2-definedness (2026-11-08): the RUNG2-mod-symbol note above says nothing is proved of the free quotient and remainder at `n == 0`; that held for facts about them, but not for terms that cancel them (`(x mod n)*0`, `x mod n - x mod n`), and a refutation could pick `n = 0`. Relations under products now carry the condition that no operation fails. Found on the way, both pre-existing and unchanged: a callee that reads an argument holding a quotient by a term is outside rung 2's domain (`f(x mod n)` gives no relation, with or without this change), and `presburger::entails` on a goal of k conjuncts each reading a remainder auxiliary grows faster than O(k log k) (54 times the bytes from k = 16 to 128 with no condition), which the condition, k more conjuncts, makes 16.2 times the instructions where translation alone is 7.4. The O(n²) cases of `Defined::meet` and `Defined::arm` (large shared divisor sets) and the 2^k reading of nested calls whose arguments may fail are fixed (treap union, call key with the arguments' conditions); `Scoped::relation` lacked the condition too and now states it.
- L1.38, PRES-mod-conjuncts (2026-11-08): the cost the RUNG2-definedness note above found on k conjuncts each reading a remainder by a term came from the reading of `&&` chains as nested `if`s (the condition held each prefix's negation) and from `settle`'s repair reading every definition that shares an atom with a disjunct; both fixed, 8.2 times the instructions at 8k. The guarded chain `(n + i == 0 || x mod (n + i) >= 0)` is still 130 times at 8k, by the existing tradeoff at `probe` (one whole `settle` per probed disjunct); it waits on conflict explanations from `settle`.
- L1.38, PRES-guarded-chain (2026-11-09): the guarded chain is now 9.1 times the instructions at 8k: `probe` settles each disjunct with only the disjunctions linked to it through a private atom before it seeks a point, and probes the disjunctions cheapest linked test first. Conflict explanations from `settle` remain the complete solution for refutations that need more than one linked disjunction.
- L1.38, PRES-nest-empty (2026-11-09): a disjunction's implied rows are now read from the deep hulls of its disjuncts, through every level of a nest, so a nest of 512 levels whose every path is empty is answered false at linear cost (it was refused from 8 levels). `Parts::atoms` was quadratic on nests of shared parts and is now linear on them, also where two shared disjunctions per level differ in their atoms; formulas whose atoms no structure tells apart are now tested against the implied rows too, so such empty nests are answered false rather than refused; this also proves the sum of two 0-or-1 conditionals `<= 2` with no join, which two ladder tests expected refused and now expect proved.
- L1.38, PROJECT-hull-credit-lower (2026-11-09): `project_parts` first removes each disjunct whose own rows put one form outside the values left to it (`values::drop_outside_values`), with or without `sets`, and on the old path, since it asks the solver nothing; the test reads each form alone (a sum of forms with gaps is not read, `// Complexity tradeoff:` there). `drop_outside_values` takes the rows of each disjunct through a function, so `values.rs` does not import `Parts` from `presburger.rs` (`s_01f_import_graph` allows no cycle).
- L1.38, TIGHTEN-each-whole (2026-11-09): the tightening of `project_parts` stays in `presburger.rs`, not a submodule, since it reads `Parts`-level helpers (`absorbed`, `disjunction_hulls`, `decide_kept`) of its parent and `s_01f_import_graph` allows no cycle. `struct Ends` was taken (the pair of bounds at `difference_ends`), so the per-group state is `Hull`. Questions asked of a symbol's group alone are exact only when every other group has a point, so a group that the solver refuses sends every symbol back to the whole formula.
- L1.38, PRES-below-key (2026-11-09): F7a as the audit proposed it (key `Below` by the base projected onto the disjunct's atoms) was already in place; the projection was not exact, since a parity witness it cannot remove stays in a row whose constant depends on the path. The fix puts the free atoms of each projected base in one form by integer shifts. Kernels that differ in other ways (two free atoms in a row, a sign change, a disjunct with a product) still miss the memo and stay 2^k on such nests; no refusal (F7b) was added. Two linked nests read as sets project `x0` to `{0}`, a sound over-approximation of the empty set (the sum `x[k] + y[k]` is even on every path), before and after this change.
- LR1: the failures of the last, failed expansion stay in `far` and `expected`. That pass reaches the operator a flat `*` loop stops at, so it records what the loop records; dropping them would lose operators from the messages. docs/plan_dag.md's wording says the opposite and its aim, unchanged messages, is met: with `Additive` and `Multiplicative` made left-recursive in a trial copy, `errors.rs` passed, and 3 of the 323 bracketing cases differed, each a flat chain now nested to the left. On that trial copy a parse took the same time per token as the flat rules (5.2 µs). The real grammar with no left recursion is no slower than before LR1 (3.8 to 5.1 µs per token against 4.1 to 5.2 µs, under load).
- LR1, for LR2: as in the paper, `E = E '+' E | N` gives a right-associative tree, so a rung must use the form `E = E '+' T | T`. A loop written in a left-recursive rule before a token that fails is walked again at each growth, so such a prefix must be a rule of its own (COMPLEXITY.md F35). A left-recursive cycle of two or more rules under a long list makes the same quadratic walk at each growth at the list's own token, so each rung must be directly left-recursive. The first alternative that matches ends a growth: with `Sum = Attempt | Sum '+' INT` and `Attempt = Sum 'q'`, a match of `Attempt` is kept on the next growth, so `Sum '+' INT` is not tried after it (a case in `leftrec.txt`).
- LR1: an entry that reads no seed is no longer matched again, which changes one thing: a rule first matched inside `!` keeps no failures, so a later read of its entry records none, as in a parser with no left recursion. As first built, a growth at that token re-recorded them. On random grammars 0.06% of error reports lost expected items or moved `far` back, never forward, and trees did not change; with no `!` in the grammars, 6.24 million comparisons showed no difference. The real grammar parses in the same time as before (4.4 to 5.9 µs per token against 4.4 to 5.7 µs, alternating runs under load).
- LR2: a marked alternative makes no node, so a `~R` whose layer is above the lowest layer of `R` reports the layer of `R`. `Grammar::read` refuses it after all rules are read, and `LitType = SignedLit L10` carries the layer that `~SignedLit L10` lost. `an_alternative_past_its_ring_is_not_tried_through_a_mark` now gives its rule `T` the layer L5, since its old grammar is refused.
- LR2: skip marks. The plan's motive, fixed parentheses and punctuation, does not hold: a literal already makes no node in either parser. The noise was the ladder of about 14 one-child nodes per expression. Options scored: `~R` on a rule name at the top of an alternative, 9, one written mark, one reader rule, a node dropped exactly where the mark stands; a `skip(e)` that drops a child, 2, nothing to drop; splicing a node's children into its parent, 3, the ladder node stays; collapsing every alternative of a single reference, 4, implicit, and it would change which forms name a layer. `~R` was applied.
- LR2: `Update = Name ('.' Name)* '=' Expr L2 | KeyPath '=' Expr L5` keeps its first alternative unchanged, because a `Path` there would lose the label role of its names. `Annotated` moved before `UnitAnnot`.
- LR2: `Expr` and `Expr12` still give one node each over a lone operand, since they are no plain pass (`Expr12 = Or ElseTail*`). The fuzz of `tools/grammar` reports `('Annotated', 2)` as never exercised; `cases.txt` covers that line by a new case.
- LR2: the tests leak the syntax tree of a chain of a million operators, because `Drop` of a deep `Expr` still recurses. T2-parse removes that recursion. The depth a parse reaches changes a little with the grammar: at a 2 MiB stack, nested calls overflow at 163 levels against 171 before, parentheses at 206 against 183.
- LR4: `Expr12`'s lone-operand alternative is now `~Or`, so a lone operand leaves no `Expr12` node (`a_name_leaves_no_node_on_the_rungs_of_the_ladder` now expects `["Expr", "Name"]`); the LR2 note above about `Expr12` giving a node no longer holds. The joins Planning bullet of DESIGN sec:joins said mixed join kinds need parentheses, which the grammar never required; it now says that `&&` and `\|\|` do not mix and a chain of `&&` kinds joins from the left, as `-` subtracts.
- LR4: the tests are in `l01_08_parser/lr4_assoc.rs`, not a folder `tests/steps/lr4_assoc/`, because a step folder's name must be a step (`is_step_name`). The fuzz reports `('JoinExpr', 1)` as never exercised, in addition to `('Annotated', 2)` and `('JoinExpr', 0)` before: `JoinExpr` is read only inside a lookahead.
- L1.39 (DESIGN.md L1.39): reductions until a round changes nothing; a type widens to its
  whole base type; only a name whose finite set lists its integers is enumerated, and a
  constraint whose form does not show it ends removes nothing (docs/thresholds.md 8); enumerations remembered per constraint and static values; a
  false static constraint gives bottom; a test's linear relation is kept only when it needs no
  auxiliary variable; the walk to the arms skips tests, function bodies and patterns;
  `zed_kernel::on_stack`, a no-op, was deleted by T2-ty. The
  `isPrime` example waits for L3. The preimage transfer remembers each (term, scope) result.
  Replacement 5 removed `CALL_DEPTH` and `TRANSFER_FUEL`: a call of a lambda whose call is
  being read stops (`StopKind::Recursion`), so calls nest no deeper than the number of
  lambdas; a call whose input-reading arguments are integers is summarized once per lambda,
  scope, landmark-snapped argument intervals and snapped demand, and its preimage is the
  summary's box met with each argument's preimage (docs/thresholds.md §5). A summary keeps
  only the intervals it narrowed its inputs to: one first computed inside another call kept
  that call's parameter box and cut points elsewhere, while claiming exact. The linear-relation
  translation remembers each call by lambda, scope and argument forms (COMPLEXITY.md S15).
- L1.39a (DESIGN.md L1.39a): the checker has no int ranges at L1 (`int[..]` and `i32` are L10), so the domain of each operand is decided as `^`'s exponent is, from its listed values and what its text shows (`Ck::known`: literals, names bound by `name = e`, `+ - * div mod ^`, the bit words, constants folded by the kernel); an int from input that no test bounds is rejected (COMPLEXITY.md C26); since NARROW-if, a test bounds it in the arm where it holds (`if n >= 0 { popCount(n) }`, `Ck::ints_here`). `exponent` now reads names through `Ck::known` too, so `k = 2 + 1; 2 ^ k` is accepted. `w: i32 = shl(1, 30)` and `x.bitAnd(255)` with `x : int[0..]` are tested on `store::interval::bit_word`, the transfer the store's product applies, since L1 has no `i32` annotation. An int literal at `f64Bits`'s `f64` parameter is the `f64` it names. Two failures combine as under every strict word (`rotl(#a, #b, width: 8)` is `#a + #b`'s value). No axioms of the bit words were added to the prelude. A binder's value is read by `Ck::known` only when a bit word or an exponent reads its name, so an unread constant such as `x = 3 ^ 30000000 + 5 ^ 30000000;` is never folded, and `Ck::known` reads children before parents on an explicit stack: `l01_39a_bit_words::deep` reads `popCount` through a chain of 20,000 bindings on an 8 MiB stack (a recursive `Ck::known` overflows it). The checker's scaling tests run on a 512 MiB stack, since the parser and the checker recurse once per nested call.
- L1.39b (DESIGN.md L1.39b): a derivation is still built when its error is made, not when it is printed, since every error the checker keeps is reported (`run::placed` prints each one's steps), but for the first run's errors that a replay of a recursive need drops, whose derivations are still built; what changed is that nothing a derivation reads is put into words before then, and that a repair trial, whose errors are only counted, builds none. A type shown through `Ck::show` in an origin keeps the carriers of its classes at the moment it was recorded (`Masks`), so the printed text is that of before. `exact_steps` stays 0 for every unit because no checker code calls the store yet (wt/xv/SYNTHESIS.md); the exact test builds `Scope`s directly. A program of 2,400 functions each calling the one before overflows an 8 MiB stack in `run::load` (found while writing the scaling test, not caused by this step; the test calls the first function from each instead). The 300-function scaling test does not see a step that grows with the origins recorded before it (L1.39b verify#1 control 2 passed it), as each function costs the checker about 1.7 million instructions; `checking_functions_of_many_parameters_scales` (L1.39b-origin-scale) measures the check alone over 100 and 800 functions of 40 parameters, about 10,000 instructions per origin, and that control fails it at 51.3x. A binding `y = x * 2` or `y = y0 + 1` costs the checker about 1.4 million instructions and 210 KB, linear in their number but large; not looked into here.
- L1.39c (DESIGN.md L1.39c): `utf8` keys its family by byte offset from 0, as the array display `[a, b]` (sec:grammar ArrayExpr), the string types (sec:order) and `p::bytes` are keyed (UTF8-keying, 2026-11-11; it was keyed from 1 before, which DESIGN had written with no author decision behind it); `fromUtf8` reads the values in key order and ignores the keys, so `{3 -> 105, -2 -> 104}` gives "hi" (DESIGN L1.39c: the bytes read in key order). At L1 the surface has no family or array display (layer L3), so the `fromUtf8` tests of hand-built byte lists run on kernel terms. The checker types a family as `(int ->? int)` with no int range (L10), so at L1 no surface form reads a byte of `utf8` into a bit word (`utf8(s)[1]` is refused: `[1]` takes a tuple). Only a written call of `codePoint` gets the interval `0 ..= 1114111` in `Ck::known` (C28); the reduced product's transfer (`store::product`) gives `codePoint` no interval. A non-int value in `fromUtf8`'s family is a type error, and an int outside `0 ..= 255` is `#badUtf8`.
- L1.19 and L1.19a (DESIGN.md sec:ports): a `Lines` input, `lines()`, `s.lines` and `m.args` are keyed from 0, the first line or word after `--` at key 0 and the last of `n` at `n - 1`, a read outside `0..<n` `#outOfBounds` (KEYS-from-zero; author, 2026-11-12: every family read forward is keyed from 0, and only `sim::framesFromEnd` counts back from its end). A line that is not UTF-8 is `#ioError("read", port, "the line at key K is not UTF-8")`, and a command-line argument that is not UTF-8 is a usage error naming its key in `m.args`; a word before `--` is still named by its place among zedc's own words, counted from 1, since that message describes zedc's command line to a person.
- Checker performance (L1.38): the elaboration retried each carrier combination with full
  derivations, so a sum of five inputs took 23.7 s; the trial runs are now quiet and only a
  shown failure is re-run with its derivation (3.7 s; the step tests 55 s → 45 s; snapshots
  unchanged).
- Known limits of the M0.5 store: the order and the stabilization recurse as deep as the graph
  (revisit at L1.24, where real programs give large graphs). Interval ends were 64-bit and
  rounded outward past that range; since TD-ends they are exact at any size (`End::Fin(Num)`,
  docs/thresholds.md replacement 10).
- OSP-order: the key of DESIGN.md M0.5 was (name, content address, canonical form), which is
  not total: two fact cells of one static node at different keypaths tie. Since ORDER-keypath
  (question A2, option A) the keypath of the fact address is the fourth part, so two cells tie
  only at one fact address, a defect of the store, which `iterate::order` refuses with
  `SameKey` naming both cells' source spans (`Equations::span`). The checker (`check/mod.rs`)
  does not call `store::iterate` yet, so no checked program reaches the refusal; `wto` and
  `iterate` are the only places that compute an order of iteration.
- The kernel `fold` term carries the depth of the folded family (M0.10). The evaluator cannot
  read the depth off a family with no leaves, so without it `fold` of an empty two-level
  family gave `#empty` where its type gives the empty family, and laws 4 and 8 failed on the
  empty input. Typing supplies the depth; a leaf at another depth is the mixed-depth error.
- Kernel values are normalized: a key over an empty level is dropped, so the nonempty-level
  conditions of laws 1, 2 and 7 have no counterexample among values. They constrain the
  guaranteed domains, and are checked where `card` facts are (L1.24, L3.6).
- Fuel and nesting depth are limits of the reference evaluator and not a meaning (spec
  reference semantics (i), commit after a1ed53b); numbers have no size limit since CAP-bits. Law 11
  deletes a dead binding whose computation would pass a limit; that is not a counterexample,
  and the laws are checked on instances the evaluator can run.
- The harness compares outcomes as values (floats bitwise after NaN canonicalization) or as
  errors of one kind, since two sides that both collide may name different keypaths.
- Joins and conjunctions in the reduced product (ST, repair 4). A join replaces the conjuncts
  of a changed block in place (`Conjuncts::swap`, `Blocks::replace`): removing them first cut
  a linked chain's tree and built the whole component's blocks again, so joins one after
  another were quadratic. A conjunct of no names is decided when it joins the relation, and a
  false relation empties the scope; `!(t >= 0)` is stored as `-1 - t >= 0`; and a conjunction
  at the root whose whole has no linear relation is narrowed side by side. With these,
  `assume(a && b)` on names apart is never wider than `a` then `b`, and is sometimes
  narrower, which is sound. The tree sizes in `Blocks` are not reduced as conjuncts leave;
  they only choose which tree is rerooted, so balance and not results depends on them.
- Complementary disjuncts (ST, repair 5). `Formula::or` returns `true` for a disjunction that
  holds two complements, `g` and `!g` or `t >= 0` and `s >= 0` with `t + s` constant and at
  least -1, decided by a hash lookup of the negated term, not by the solver. A conjunct
  removed from a block of names whose other conjuncts still link its names is handled by
  placing those conjuncts again (`Blocks::split`); the union-find of trees cannot split, so
  any removal that would split a tree still rebuilds the component.

- L2.1: a display in body position (a lambda, `else` or arm body) without parentheses gets the parser's general "expected …" message, as the grammar's `(Block | !'{' Expr)` gives; the spec calls it a parse error whose repair is parentheses, and a message naming that repair is open. Two paths of one `with` clause where one is a prefix of the other (`c = …, c.x = …`) are accepted: the spec rejects only identical paths and does not state this case. The formatter prints `(p with { x = 1 }).x` with parentheses, since `.x` after the braces belongs to the `with`. A struct name used as a value or type before L2.4 is reported as not defined. The tests `l01_10`, `l01_11` and `l01_14` changed: a parenthesized display and a tuple parameter now build L2 forms, and the fences accept the refusal " is compiled from step L2.…". Four pins of `l01_29_diagnostics::variants` moved: those programs now parse past their struct or `type` line and stop at `-> int` (L10) or `match` (L2.2).
- L2.2: an empty `match` (`match x {}`) is a syntax error, since `Match` reads `nest(Arm % ',' ','?)`, which needs one arm; the spec does not say whether an empty match over an empty type is allowed. Two equal annotations on one declaration (`@memoized @memoized f = …`) are not rejected, and annotation arguments are not resolved, since every annotation is refused for now; the layer that builds each must decide both. `...` in annotation arguments is refused. A refused pattern binds nothing, so a use of its name in the arm body also gives "`n` is not defined", as at L2.1. The formatter writes every `match` one arm a line, even a short one. The corpus test of `l01_13_formatter::fences` asserts the exact layout of every program that builds except `10-regex-matcher.zed` (layer L19), named in the test: it builds past its import now, and its `hhmm` record display is wrapped by hand, so the corpus or the formatter's line wrapping must change when L19 resolves. The tests `l01_13_formatter::layout` (two new cases), `l01_29_diagnostics::variants` (the payload-by-position program now stops at its `type` line, L2.5) and the step index snapshot of `m0_01_scaffolding` changed.
- L2.3: a unit's imports are found by resolving it once alone (`resolve::Alone`), before its imported units are known; the loader then resolves it again against them, so each unit is resolved twice on its first load (both linear). The binder of a type parameter or of a pattern field `f:` is the whole declaration or pattern, as for every binder (`Binder::span`), since the AST keeps no span per parameter or field. A field written twice in a struct is rejected by the AST builder (L2.1), before resolution. A `match` reported as a later form does not report its arms' patterns again, and the ends of a range pattern are part of the range (the `l03_01_parser::later` expectations). `zedc run` reads a package only when the unit has an import or the manifest names a prelude, so a single file under a manifest runs as before. The tests `l01_11_statements` (`local` in a block now builds), `l01_14_name_resolution`, `l01_29_diagnostics::binder_type`, `l02_01_parser_structs::later`, `l02_02_parser_match_imports::later` and the step index snapshot of `m0_01_scaffolding` changed; the snapshot also gains `l01_19a_command_line` and `l01_39b_on_demand`, which were missing from it at a9330ae7. The resolution key holds the number the database gives each import's exports, not a BLAKE3 digest of them, since L1.37a keeps hashes out of keys (repair 1, at the rebase onto 0b7ff697). The scaling test of many empty roots is the one a linear scan in `unit::add` fails (47.2 times the instructions); the other five pass with it.
- LR4-fix: LR4 was merged after a rebase onto L2.1 without a test run; at its own base no display read `Expr12`'s node, so its tests passed. Any builder that tells kids apart by rule name over a position where `Expr12` (or another `~` rule) stands has the same hazard; `display` was the only one found (the other rule-name tests in `ast` read `Update`, `PlainArg`, `Item`, `Params`, `ArrowParams`, `Type` and `FieldPat`, none of which a pass alternative yields). Negative control: the old rule-name test put back fails 7 tests of `l02_01_parser_structs`, the 3 reported and 4 of the 5 new ones (the fifth checks the refusal of a field given twice, which both pass).
- L3.1: `not (a in b)` is a syntax error, since Zed negates with `!` (`!(a in b)`); `a in b in c` is a syntax error, since `InTest` does not chain. `(..<)` is a syntax error: a range operator is not a `BinOp`. Nested parentheses around a section build one section, `((+))` is `(+)`. `[int]` in an expression is an array display of the name `int`, and a type only in type position. `{ x }` is a set and `{}` the empty map, as Display precedes Block in Primary. A `for` body must export: `for x in m { g(x); }` stops at its expression statement (L6). The formatter writes a `for` in parentheses as the operand of an operator and as a `for` source or guard, which the grammar does not need; `if` and `match` operands are still written bare (`if a { 1 } else { 2 } + 1`), as before. With the forms of L3 building, ten more corpus programs build and format to a fixed point, and each differs from its text only by hand layout the formatter does not do (`=` and trailing comments aligned, long lines wrapped, a `match` on one line in `23-join-zoo.zed`), listed in `l01_13_formatter::fences`; the corpus or the formatter must change for the test to compare them. Tests changed: `l01_08_parser::deep` (a spread suffix, L6, in place of a display at the bottom of a deep nest), `l01_09_postfix_chains::calls` (`unordered`, L9, in place of `::len`), `l01_11_statements::blocks` (`({ x })` is now a set), `l01_14_name_resolution::fences` (accepts " is compiled from step L3." and later-layer annotations, since fences using L3 forms now build), `l02_01_parser_structs::blocks` (sets and maps build), the step index snapshot of `m0_01_scaffolding`.
- L6.1: The grammar has no labeled `break`: a loop's name names its step index, and `break` ends the innermost loop, so `break i` in an inner loop is a break with the outer step as its value. `p'.x = 1;` and `p.x' = 1;` parse as method declarations (`T.m = e`); resolution refuses them as primed names (L6.3). The lexer takes one prime per name: `x''` is a lexical error. `x = 1 with;`, `x[] = 0;` and `break y -> y` are syntax errors. The statement order of a block is normalized in the builder as well as the formatter, so a text and its formatted text build to the same statements; the s-expression of a block lists `while` guards first and `until` guards last. A block that ends in an expression statement exports nothing, so `for x in m { g(x); }` and `x -> { y = x; y; }` now fail with "this block exports nothing" where they failed with "this form (ExprStmt) is built from layer L6". `a*.5` lexes `*.` as one token and is a syntax error ("expected IDENT"); `a * 0.5` is the product. With `loop` and indexed definitions building, nine more corpus programs build and format to a fixed point, each differing from its text only by hand layout, listed in `l01_13_formatter::fences`; three of them (15, 24, 28) write a `while` guard after the step, where DESIGN line 428 has the formatter write it first, so the corpus or that rule should change. Tests changed: `l01_08_parser::deep` (`unordered`, L9, in place of a spread suffix), `l01_09_postfix_chains::calls` (the spread case dropped), `l01_11_statements::blocks` (the exports-nothing error; a keyed push, L7, in place of a boundary), `l03_01_parser::later` (the exports-nothing error), `l01_13_formatter::fences` (the nine programs), `l01_14_name_resolution::fences` (accepts " is compiled from step L6."), the step index snapshot of `m0_01_scaffolding`.
- L25.8: The brief says "no other skipping" than the optimizer-equal mutants. A mutant can turn a program whose rows end into one that never ends: `w(positional f) = f(f); guard(positional x) = if x > 0 { w(w) } else { x } test { 0 -> 0 }` ends, and its mutant with `0` replaced by `-1` takes the `w(w)` branch, so `zedc test` on the mutated text did not end in 20 s (killed, exit 124). With no recursion at L1 the only source of such a loop is self-application, but a runner without a budget (docs/thresholds.md) cannot stop it. So a mutant's rows run only when `stage::ends` admits each closed term, and a mutant with a row it does not admit is counted "not run" and printed with its position. The cost: a higher-order call through a parameter (`twice(f: inc, x)`) is not admitted, so its definition's mutants are not run. The front end, the mixer and term equality recurse, so a chain of 800 additions needs the 8 MiB main stack (`zedc` runs on it; the scaling test uses `on_main_sized_stack`); `mutate`'s own walks use explicit stacks. `Info.quotients` records each `*` whose product the checker types with no `int` (`rat` or `f64`), where `/` is defined; `*` on `int` has no `/` mutant. Tests changed, since every step's `zed/` unit is run by the L1 harnesses and the new `fares.zed` adds 7 checks: `l01_33_lowering::corpus` (53 rows, 65 lowered terms), `l01_34_memory::corpus` and `l01_36_cranelift::corpus` (53 rows; 65 terms, 117 cells, 121 or 147 writes), `l01_37_oracle::every_step_unit_agrees` (130 native runs, 14 compared), the usage line in `l01_21_test_runner::command`, and the step index snapshot of `m0_01_scaffolding`. `tools/run_tests.sh 4`: 98 pieces, 1 failed, `l01_29_diagnostics::printed::every_printed_type_parses_back_to_itself` (25 `#ioError(_)` types of L1 units, failing on main since 4d82672, item L29-print).
- OSP-lit: read failures now carry `#ioError(op, path, why)`, replacing the bare `#ioError` of the L1.19 note above; the types still print the atom as `#ioError(_)` at L1. The path of a `Lines` port's error is the port's name. A bare pattern `#a` in `else` matches `#a` with any payload or none (DESIGN L1.27 allows it). A doc link resolves against every binder of the unit and the prelude, not by scope. An unattached doc block is an error, since the checker has no warnings. A float literal is limited by its rounded value only; the cost of reading the digits of a long int or rat literal is that of `num-bigint`'s decimal parse, which is quadratic in the digits (not changed here).
- OSP-drop: the statement-position parts (a statement `e else d;` and `*.`) are left to L6.3. The match arm `_ ->` is a pattern, not a binding (DESIGN.md's table of `_`), and `match` arrives at L2.4, so the test checks only that it is refused as L2.4 and not as a drop. `(_, x) = …` is not a binding at L1 (`TupleParam` is L2), so nested `_` is tested as the target list `_, x = …`. The repair note writes `_ = … else #ok;` and does not quote the value, since the checker has no source text and `Expr`'s display is prefix form. A default that is not an atom literal (a name, a call) names no atoms: its own loose atoms are walked like any other value's.
- OSP-drop2: a name bound by `name = e` now carries the naming of `e`: `y = lookup(1) else #notFound; _ = y;` is accepted, where OSP-drop rejected it. The set kept per expression may hold more atoms than its type, where a part's failure stops there (`==` gives a `bool`); `_` keeps only those of the type it binds, so the extra atoms can only reject. `Ty::dropped` is no longer used by the checker, only by `discard.rs`. The match criterion is written as an ignored test, since resolve refuses `match` until L2.4. `l01_29_diagnostics::printed::every_printed_type_parses_back_to_itself` fails on this branch and on its base b9115b2 alike (25 printed types such as `#ioError(_)` hold a form of layer L2); it is not caused here.
- L1.19a: DESIGN did not say how a `main` test row gives a `CommandLine` port; it is a `String` with one argument per line, split as a `Lines` input is, so an argument holding a newline cannot be given by a row (the spec sentence is on `wt/l1-19a-spec`). Words of other `zedc` commands that are not UTF-8 are usage errors too, since `main.rs` now reads `args_os`. The record without its program's content address, noted here, was fixed by L1.19b.
- L1.19b: DESIGN (step L1.19) says a record names "the content address of its program" without saying what is hashed. The implementation hashes the canonical address of the term a wave runs (`main` closed over the definitions it reaches, under the prelude) and the ports' text, so two programs that differ only in local names or layout share one address, and a change to a function `main` does not reach keeps it. The address is taken once per program at its first wave, O(t log t), also when nothing is recorded. Settled 2026-11-05 by the orchestrator: the address covers the term `main` runs and the port declarations, since a function `main` does not reach cannot change a run; DESIGN step L1.19 says so on `wt/l1-19b-spec`.
- CHK-cost (with CHK-curried and CHK-carrier; COMPLEXITY F77): nested tuples n^3 -> linear (39k instructions per node), nested lambdas n^2 -> linear (62k per node), `+` 1.1M -> 140k instructions per node, negation 390k -> 65k, call 340k -> 80k. Type variables keep their class name until `finish` writes the names once, so curried lambdas using every parameter are linear (8.4 times the instructions, 8.2 times the bytes at n = 100 and 800). A class solved to a carrier is replaced outside the lambdas only and read through the union-find inside them (`Ck::stale`): curried lambdas whose parameters take a carrier 8.0 times the instructions and 7.9 times the bytes (n^2 before), test no longer ignored; a chain of calls `g(0)(1)…(n)` is linear by a memoized `Sig::digest`. Repair 5: `is` tests compare such lambdas through the resolver (`Ty::diff_with`); before, the branch where a tuple holding one is not of the tested type kept it, in programs already rejected because a tuple takes no function. `curried_classes` checks 25 programs against the output of the build that replaces classes at every depth. Open: a held function at the bottom of n nested tuples is n^2 in its error notes (ledger CHK-held-cascade).
- CHK-held-cascade (COMPLEXITY F89): the error for a function held in a tuple is now given once, at the tuple expression that holds it (`Ty::unchecked_function`), not again where the value flows through more tuples, bindings or calls; this changes which span the error names when a tuple is made inside a called function from its argument (the call that binds it, `wrap(scale)`). Left for the author, as each is a choice of what a message shows: n separate tuple expressions holding one function are n real errors whose derivations repeat O(n) notes each, O(n^2) in all; one error through n nested tuples of data has 2n notes each printing a subtuple, O(n^2) text; a type that shares a row at each level prints in 2^n characters. The whole check of a type 2,000 tuples deep still overflows a 2 MiB stack in `zed_kernel::types::empty::Search::rep` (T2-types-rest); `Ty::kernel`, `replace_in` and `subst` still recurse once a level (T2-ty).
- CHK-need-uses: the destructuring need is a tuple of exactly `n`, as the run's `TupleGet` needs, so a longer tuple is rejected rather than read by its first `n` components. The rejection has no row in `zed/fences/rejections.txt`, as the tuple-index need has none. A need that names a variable the call leaves unbound (a generic function passed as an argument) was measured at the merge and was quadratic twice over: `check::bound` copied the call's binds at each such need, and `Ty::replace_in` scanned every bound variable at each signature it met (that scan was on main before this item); both are fixed (COMPLEXITY F90). Open, not measured: when a signature does hold a bound variable, `Ty::replace_in` still builds the binds that are not its own by a pass over all of them.
- CHK-index-else: `r(fs, args, k) = fs[args[k]]`, with no `else`, is still rejected with "this function, which `r` applies, does not take #notFound, and no argument of this call gives it". Rule 6 passes an atom by when an argument of the call gives it; `args` is a `CommandLine`, whose reads give `#notFound`, but the checker counts only the atoms at the top of an argument's type, not those its reads give. Whether rule 6 counts the atoms of what a function-valued argument gives is an author question. Also, `g(r) = r else 0` keeps its parameter's variable whole (`(r: _) -> 0 | _`), so `g(r: args[1])` still holds `#notFound`: an over-approximation for a parameter that may hold any value, left as it was.
- ROW-made-cost (COMPLEXITY F93): `Row::made` merged two mostly overlapping variable sets by inserting each variable of the smaller, O(n^2 log n) over n rows `t(k) = (t(k-1), (t(k-1), Vk))` (70.6 times the instructions at 250 and 2,000); `check::ty::merge` now steps `imbl::OrdSet::diff` over the shared nodes in turn with the insertions, 10.0 times. Rows merging two sets that share no node (`z(k) = (x(k), y(k))`) stayed O(n^2 log n) under author question A8; CK-data-memo closed it by keeping bits per row, not sets (8.3 times at 250 and 2,000, was 71.2). Found: `Ty::replace_in` walks a shared row once per path, 2^n on `p(s, v) = (s, (s, v))` nested n deep (ledger REPLACE-shared-rows).
- ATOM-payload-fn (COMPLEXITY F95): an atom whose payload holds a function is refused by `==`, `!=` and `String` and as a tuple component, at any depth of payloads; the refusal of `==` now has the derivation of its operand, so `==` and `String` messages that had no notes now have some. Open: `held_wide` on wt/atom-payload-sub needs the same walk; `Row::open` ignores payload variables, so a payload built from a parameter and returned in an export tuple escapes the check (ATOM-payload-open); `#a(#a(…))` n deep is O(n^2), pre-existing; fixed by ATOM-nested-sq (F106).
- CONST-wide-addr (COMPLEXITY Z26): an exact number past `i64` is addressed by its sign and the 64-bit limbs of its numerator and denominator in lowest terms, not by its decimal digits, so `canon::VERSION` is 4 and three pinned addresses changed. A power of 2 kept in a `Rat` is built by a shift; a power of an odd prime is still built by num-bigint's squaring, above O(n log n), as before.
- REPLACE-shared-rows (COMPLEXITY F97): the rebuilding walks of a type (`replace_in`, `subst`, `settle`) keep a memo of the rows they made, by address, and `Ck::data` and `vars_outside` a set of the rows they entered. The program family `p(s, v) = (s, (s, v))` nested n deep was O(n^2) (not approved, A20), since each call replayed its data need on its argument, a type of k rows at the kth call (`Ck::data`), and `bound` read the argument's k variables; CK-data-memo fixed it with memos keyed by node number in `Ck::data` and `Ck::bound`, kept in the undo log, and an index kept by each binding (`Binds`). The walks still recurse once per level (T2-ty): the scaling test of the walks uses 100 and 800 levels because 2,000 overflow a 2 MiB stack. Part 3, for question A8: the per-row variable sets cannot all be replaced by the memoized walk. The replacing walks (`holds_any`, `Replacer::holds`) only prune with them and would stay linear in the type without them, given the memo; but `bound`, `solved`, `settled`, `names`, `meet`'s `has_vars`, `hold`'s `facts().holds`, `first_seen`'s pruning, `Sig::settle` and `finished`'s empty test, and `VarFacts::of`'s `free` read them per need, call or signature, so a walk there costs O(size of the type) per query where the set costs O(1) or O(log n): the program family would go from O(n^2) to more. What they read is mostly a yes or no (any class, any name, any bound variable) and the next free name, which a per-row flag and a per-row largest variable number give in O(1) without the sets of F93's disjoint case; `facts().holds(x)` and the variable lists `bound`, `solved` and `settled` need are what remain, and those a memoized walk answers in the size of the type.
- ATOM-nested-sq (COMPLEXITY F106): a payload shape is shared, as a row is, and keeps what it holds at any depth, so atoms nested in atoms are checked in linear time; code that builds a `Shape` calls `Shape::new` and reads its items and fields through `Deref`, and cannot change them in place. With a function n atoms deep, the refusal of `==` still prints O(n^2) characters (2^n for a payload held twice), as F89 (b) and (c) for tuples, open for the author.
- TUPLE-eq-dup (COMPLEXITY F109): `RowData` keeps the kernel type of its tuple shape, made in `Row::made`, replacing the `shape_kernel` walk; the field is a plain `Option<KType>`, since a lazily filled `OnceLock` in a row used as a map key fails clippy's `mutable_key_type`. Rows that hold a variable or the unknown keep none, as before.
- ATOM-payload-open (COMPLEXITY row ATOM-payload-open): a variable, the unknown or a function in an atom's payload inside a tuple is held by the tuple at any depth (`Row::open`, `Row::dynamic`, `Ty::closed`, `Ty::kernel`), so the data need of `==` on a returned row reaches the parameter whose variable sits in a payload. A row's `open` and `dynamic` are read through `Ty::closed` and `Ty::holds_unknown` of each component, which read rows and payload shapes at their outer level.
- TY-subst-stacks (COMPLEXITY row TY-subst-stacks): `subst`, `replace_in`, `settle` and the drop of a type keep their own stack, so a type of any depth is replaced, settled and dropped on a 2 MiB stack; results and visit order are unchanged.
- T2-types-rest-4 (COMPLEXITY K39): the `Debug` text of a type changed where a `Type` is shared, and so did the numbers of diagram nodes and expressions: a type that holds other types (one with an atom, whose payload is a type, or a tuple or morphism part that is not a leaf) and is reached twice or more is written once as `#k=Type(..)` and then as `#k#`, and `k` counts from 0 over the whole text in the order written, where part 3 counted from 0 in each part. Types are told apart by value (the type's digest and comparison), not by address, so equal types built apart get one number and the text stays a function of the type, as zedc's query keys need. Types that hold no other type (`int`, a literal, a recursive type) are written in full each time, as before. The 28 sample texts of `debug_text.txt` have no shared type and are unchanged. `Part` `not` and `zip` run on heap frames, 1.3 to 1.9 times the time of the recursion in a debug build.
- NARROW-hub-settle (COMPLEXITY C26): outside `@exact`, a test whose relation is a difference of two int names (`a >= n`, `n <= a`, `a - n >= 3`, and their negations) is no longer kept as a written constraint; the relation's projection of the difference gives what enumerating it gave (inferred from the spoke's projection being exact; checked by `l01_39_reduced_product::lazy` and the l01_29, l01_38, l01_39, l01_39a and l01_39b groups, all passing unchanged). A written constraint would pin its names, so they would be no leaves of a lazy scope. Equality spokes (`ai == n`) stay eager. Author questions on this item are in its ledger line.
- NARROW-hub-rest (COMPLEXITY C26): outside `@exact`, a test whose relation is a bound on a sum of int names, each of coefficient one or minus one (`a >= n + m`, `a + m >= n`, `a - n - m >= 3`, and their negations), is no longer kept as a written constraint, extending NARROW-hub-settle's rule for a difference of two names; a coefficient of two (`a >= n + n + m`) keeps it. With all names but one fixed, enumerating such a test keeps the last name on one side of a bound, which the relation's projection gives as well (inferred from that; checked by `l01_39_reduced_product::lazy` with three-name constraints and the l01_29, l01_38, l01_39, l01_39a, l01_39b and l01_39c groups, all passing unchanged). The rejection notes of `ai >= n + m` are those of before, which name `m >= -1` and `m >= -2` but not `n >= -1`; the full-derivation rule of L1.29 asks for `n >= -1`, a follow-up item, since this item keeps every note as it was.
- NARROW-hub-related (COMPLEXITY C26): a star of two hubs or more is projected together with the conjuncts among its hubs, so a test among the hubs (`n >= m`, `n + m >= 0`) leaves its leaves lazy and their product exact; without them, `n + m >= 0` would give `a0` int[-1..] where it is int[0..] (the eager-answer test fails so, checked once with the core removed). The lazy-versus-eager random test cannot see this, since both scopes project stars the same way; the eager-answer test does.
- NARROW-notes-name (DESIGN step L1.29): notes may now name fewer tests than before where a carrying test's path gives the read name its product from the other names' products at that test (the earlier tests that moved the name are dropped); the l01_29, l01_38, l01_39 and l01_39a groups pass unchanged, and the tests that count notes are in l01_39a.
- NARROW-eager-scope (DESIGN step L1.29): notes name fewer tests where a carrying test alone gives a name it read the product it carried (`m >= -2` under `m >= -1` is dropped), and name the tests of a longer path where no shortest path explains the carried name; the l01_29, l01_38, l01_39 and l01_39a groups pass with the expected sets updated in l01_39a only
- ROW-eq-deep (COMPLEXITY F118): `Ty`, `Row`, `Shape` and `Sig` compare by `Same`, a comparison on its own stack with Hopcroft and Karp's union-find over the addresses of shared nodes; `Ty`'s `Hash` is written out to match the derived one, since clippy's `derived_hash_with_manual_eq` refuses a derived `Hash` beside a written `PartialEq`. `Sig::facts` is a cache and still takes no part. The needs of a signature are still compared by `==` on each type, one comparison each, as they nest only as deep as a call's text. Addresses are keys only while both operands are borrowed.
- T2-ty (COMPLEXITY F128): `Ty::meet`, `meets` and `contains` keep their own stack and a memo by the addresses of each pair of nodes, valid while both operands are borrowed; `Debug` of `Ty`, `Row`, `Shape` and `Sig` writes the derived text from a loop, and under `{:#?}` writes the same one line, where the derived `Debug` broke it over many lines (no test or tool read that form). `zed_kernel::on_stack`, a no-op since T2-mid, is gone.
- CHK-need-bound (COMPLEXITY F123, DESIGN steps L1.17 and L1.39a): a parameter of no declared type whose value reaches `^`'s exponent on an int, or an `int[0..]` operand of a bit word, records a need `NeedKind::InDomain` (`int[0..]`, or `int[0..<2 ^ w]` under a width the checker knows), checked at each call from the argument's interval as `^`'s exponent is; a wrapper passing its own parameter on takes the need with a link, and the message lists every call down to the use. Decided here, by the rule that the checker never runs code and every run-time type error is prevented statically: a value of a type variable that is not a parameter's (a lambda's result, a tuple component) and an expression of a parameter (`f(y + 1)`) take no int outside the domain (checked on what flows into the class), and a defaulted parameter, a generic operand related to another operand (funnel shifts' `k`, a generic `width`, `byteSwap`) and a bit word used as a function value are rejected at the use, not followed. Related hole fixed: `sum` of a value of a type variable accepted a tuple of strings (now `NeedKind::Sum`, checked on what flows in). The `NoInt` message now reads "{use}, and this value may be {type}, not shown to be in {domain}".
- CARET-spacing (author, 2026-11-09; DESIGN sec:lexical, the `^` row): `^` is written without spaces, `0..=2^48`, `x * 2^k`, `(x + 1r)^2`, and spaced input parses the same. The kernel term printer (`print.rs`, `Pow`), the formatter (`format.rs`, `POWER`) and the messages and repairs that print a power (`int[0..<2^w]`, `int[0..<2^width]`, `mod 2^k`, `x^n`) write none; expected outputs changed in their spacing only. Zed examples, the corpus, README, the fence copies and Zed code spans in COMPLEXITY.md, ZED_PORT_GAPS.md and docs/thresholds.md were rewritten; STATUS.md and docs/plan_dag.md records were left as written. Not changed: the S-expression trees of the grammar cases and `show.rs` (`(^ a b)`, `(2 ^ 3)`, token dumps, not Zed text), ZIR edge text (`r^0`), corpus 28's calculator input (its own language, which splits on spaces), and Rust comments using `^` as mathematics.
- PROJECT-growth-box (merged and pushed in batch 86, 564bef57; COMPLEXITY row PROJECT-growth-box; DESIGN step L1.38, spec b908875 with DOCS-TODO 51): where the solver refuses a projection, the preimage and the scope keep the bounds of the box stage over the rows, met with the catalog's box, and still warn. The scope warnings' third step now says what is kept ("so here each of their variables keeps only the bounds that each condition gives it from the bounds of the others"; for a test, "so the test narrows the values of its variables here only to bounds that may be wider than it allows"). The relation of a refused preimage is still unused, and a refused entailment question is still reported as not proved.
- MSG-growth-projection-cause (COMPLEXITY S28; no spec change, since DESIGN and DOCS-TODO 51 hold no message text): a refused projection's warning no longer ends "with no values found and none ruled out", which was false once PROJECT-growth-box kept bounds; it ends with the bounds each variable kept, in the program's names and type syntax (`x: int[0..=9]`), names the variables left unbounded ("may still be any whole number"), or says the bounds leave no value. A refused test names the bounds found on its variables; a set-aside disjunct keeps the old sentence. A refusal met twice in a scope keeps the meet of its sets, and a join keeps their join. The random refused-projection tests now also check reversed, shuffled and rewritten orders of the items and names (a negative control, an order-dependent box, was caught by those writings in 26 cases, by none of the old ones; not committed).
- MSG-keyword-as-name (COMPLEXITY rows MSG-keyword-as-name, front end and tradeoffs; DESIGN sec:diagnostics row "Reserved word written where a name stands", sec:lexical, DOCS-TODO 114): any of the 38 keywords written where a name stands (a binding, a parameter, a function, method, field, type, struct or import name, a field after `.`, a record or named-argument field, a loop variable) is reported at the word with a one-sentence headline that shows the line and its repair, "Reserved word used as a name: `without = 3;`. Try `rest = 3;` instead." (author rule of 2026-11-12, IMPL-common item 9), and notes that say what the word begins (`without` removes a facet from a value, as `n without units("km")`) and that its other uses as a name take the new name too; when the renamed line does not parse, the headline offers the name alone ("Try another name, such as `rest`."). The table `RESERVED` in `crates/zedc-syntax/src/parse/clause.rs` gives each word what it begins and a name of like meaning, kept in the order of `KEYWORDS` by a test. The word is found by reparsing with a name in place of at most three words (the one the parse stopped at, and the last and the first before it in the statement); it is accepted when that parse gets past the stop and past the token after the word, so `y = not x;` and `x = a is ;` keep the parse's own message. This replaces the `initial`-only message of INITIAL-decl: `initial = 0;` now has the row and the new text, and `initial _ = 0;` gets the parse's own "expected a name" at `_`. The `match = 3;` case of `l01_08_parser::plain_names` changed to the new message.

Tests before (25d87b8d3) 583 pieces, 0 failed; after (rebased on 7d96d3826) 583 pieces, 1 failed, l01_29 `menu_order::each_design_example_with_a_menu_stands_in_designs_order_and_zedc_writes_it_so`, which fails on main too from spec 6ba82c3 (MSG-concise-style). - SECTION-op-enum (no COMPLEXITY row, no spec change: a refactor): `ExprKind::Section` takes `BinaryOp` in place of the operator string; the parser converts the `OpFunction` token once with `BinaryOp::of_token`, and the AST printer and the formatter print it with `as_str` and `Display`, so every printed form is unchanged. - GROUP-decide-bytes (COMPLEXITY K27; no spec change): no allocation in deciding a recursive group grows faster than n. `l01_23_subtyping::judgments::deciding_a_group_scales` decided the ring of 256 once before its check, so the first run at 256 found the group's canonical form (`Group::canon`, made on first use and kept with the group) already made while the first run at 2,048 made its own: 12.3x the bytes at 72c739f02, 11.3x on main, against the limit 12.1. ZED_PORT_GAPS entries for the treap.

New test `l01_38_presburger::ladder::products_whose_factors_one_sum_joins_scale`: 9.7 times the instructions and 7.9 times the bytes at 8 and 64 links, limit 17.6; negative control with the old per-side search, not committed: 25.4 times the bytes, failed. `l01_38_presburger` and `zedc_presburger`: 353 pieces, 0 failed, load 39 to 78. New plan row C2-pairs-long-row, feeding SCALE-cover.

Kept by the sign test: the crossed product, `x - z, x + z - w, y ⊨ 2xy >= wy` and `x - z, w + z, y ⊨ xy + wy >= 0` (`ladder::a_premise_with_a_factor_foreign_to_the_other_side_is_left_out_of_the_products`). A factor in no product is never foreign (replaced by CD-audit, below: the test is now `ladder::a_factor_cancels_through_rows_on_the_other_side_of_both_signs`). Python model: 0 of 230 entailments lost (90 without the sign test); 0 of 6,556 further random ones (the sign test alone 2, the partner condition alone 14, neither 71). `l01_38_presburger` and `zedc_presburger`: 355 pieces, 0 failed; l01_39 + l01_25: 414 pieces, 0 failed; load 35 to 70. - CD-audit (COMPLEXITY C2; no spec change): audit of the merged code that came from CD (e8fea7860, 0823e7c43 + 346407a9f, a98079c36..711b27b81, 6d5a815dd). Rewritten: the C2-pairs-long-row rule's CD condition "a factor in no product is never foreign" named the wrong cause, and adding the unrelated premise `d * q >= 0` to its own example lost the proof. `products` now asks, for a factor `u` of `a` in no product with `y`, whether another linear row `r` on a partner of `y` can cancel `u * y`, which needs `r_u × b'_y` of the other sign: `r` holds `u` with the other sign, or the rows on `y` hold `y` with both signs (found once, in one pass). Test `ladder::a_factor_cancels_through_rows_on_the_other_side_of_both_signs` (third case red on e8fea7860); new scaling test `ladder::products_whose_premise_holds_k_atoms_in_no_product_scale`, 7.8 times at 8 → 64; the two scaling tests of C2-pairs-long-row within 0.2% of their instructions before. - C2-pairs-exact (COMPLEXITY C2; no spec change): `presburger::products` leaves a product out exactly when it alone, among the products not yet left out, holds a product atom that no premise, goal or definition mentions, with a nonzero coefficient, repeated to a fixpoint (`crates/zedc-presburger/src/presburger/pairs.rs`, `kept`): exact, since such an atom can take a value that satisfies its one product, and independent of order and names. - TRIVIAL-shared-atom (COMPLEXITY C32 (1) and F131; no spec change; tests only, `tests/steps/l22_08_vacuity/`): an atom whose sides name a common field is held as the pairs of paths that agree, numbered by a walk of the left side's decision tree and, at each leaf, the right side's, and written as runs of pair numbers (`Theory::pair_form`), not as cubes; the engine keeps for each choice the list of its runs and for each variable the gaps between its nodes' runs, each list watching its first live pair over a set of live pairs (`LiveSet`). On `f1(..fd(x)..) == fd(..f1(x)..)` the default report at d = 50 and 400 went from 42 and 18,711 million instructions (442 times, cubic) to 7.6 and 539 million (71 times); `scaling::a_shared_field_atom_scales` replaces `a_shared_field_atom_is_cubic` (73.9 times the instructions, 57.6 the bytes, limit 107.8; negative control with the cubes, not committed: 466.5 times the bytes). Models, verdicts, choices and dead ends are the same in all 17,234 group reports of the corpus, 8,000 random and 300 3-SAT theories in both modes; 51 passages of the 9,495 conflict explanations list the same removals in another order or end at another field. 22 tests, `--only 'l22_08'`
- TRIVIAL-walk-index (COMPLEXITY C32 (1) and F131; no spec change; tests only, `tests/steps/l22_08_vacuity/`): the right side's tree of a shared-field atom is indexed by the keys of its leaves (`KeyIndex`): each entry, a node with one key below it, keeps its children of that key by choice, and each entry that starts a chain (the root, or a child of an entry with two or more such children) keeps the choices that every path from it to a leaf of the key makes, so the walk enters it only when the left leaf agrees (O(min(chosen, needed) log) a check; the index O(E log^2 E) for E entries). The new family `f(x, .., x) == g1(..gk(g0(f(y, .., y, x), f(y, .., y, x)))..)` (`scaling::a_shared_field_atom_with_cut_subtrees_scales`) went from 53.6 times the instructions at k = 200 and 1600 (41,617 and 2,572,817 walk steps; negative control on main's walk, not committed) to 8.2 times (6 k + 20 steps, limit 12.3); the d-family keeps its 2 d^2 + 6 d + 2 steps, 6.9 and 510 million instructions at d = 50 and 400 (main 7.2 and 535), 73.4 times, limit 107.8 (negative control with a scan of the scope at each pair, not committed: 140.0 times). Left open, plan row TRIVIAL-walk-branches: when the left leaf cuts off each child of a right branch point by a different field, the chain above it is still walked (`f1(f2(w(x, .., x), x), x) == c1(..cn(g(f1(y, x), f2(y, x)))..)`, n = 256: 1,551 pairs, 69,675 steps). 23 tests, `--doc --only '^l22_08_vacuity$'`
- TRIVIAL-walk-branches round 2 (COMPLEXITY C32 (1) and F131; no spec change; tests only, `tests/steps/l22_08_vacuity/`; ideas from the Claude seat of the hybrid cross-review): on a field both sides test, the walk enters the two children of each choice together, only for the choices whose children can hold a pair, listed once for each pair of classes from the side with fewer live children (replaces `Picks`); each side's `KeyIndex` is built at the walk's first lookup in it (built at the start it took 3.5 times main's instructions at m = 128 on atoms whose sides are distinct rotations of `h(x0..xm)`, now 1.2 times); the other tree's keys are a sorted list. Brief, wide, same and ne and their mirrors grow 7.5 to 7.8 times at m = 128 and 1024 (limit 12.6) and take at most 1.3 times main (wide mirrored, 29.4 against 22.9 million instructions); the d-family 5.2 and 252 million at d = 50 and 400, 49 times (limit 108); the cut family 15 k + 41 steps; the joint-split family 20 m^2 + 30 m + 16 steps, 54.2 times (limit 123.2). - TRIVIAL-walk-branches (COMPLEXITY C32 (1) and F131; no spec change; tests only, `tests/steps/l22_08_vacuity/`; hybrid cross-review, 2 rounds): a shared-field atom is decided by a walk over pairs of nodes, one from each side: a field fixed on one side is followed on the other; a leaf against a subtree uses its `KeyIndex` entry; on a shared field the side with fewer leaves is split, and only the children that can hold a pair are entered (`Picks`, built once per pair of classes); on different fields the side whose field the other tests further down is split, or neither; nodes of one class are walked once, dead children and keys absent from the other side are skipped, leaf groups go last, and runs are sorted by a counting sort. The eight families brief, wide, same and ne and their mirrors take 7.5 to 7.8 times the instructions at m and 8 m (limit 12.6) and at most 1.6 times main; on main 6 of the 8 fail the limit (negative control, not committed). Left open, plan row TRIVIAL-walk-picks: when every pair of classes differs (VJ3), building `Picks` is m^3 (163 million instructions at m = 64, main 171 million). 25 tests, `--only l22_08_vacuity`

- MSG-split-imports (no COMPLEXITY row: no new code; spec: DESIGN sec:diagnostics "Names the split repair adds"): the split repair's new names `f1`, `f2` (or the least free numbers) avoid only the names the refused unit writes, not those of its importers. An importer reaches a unit's names only by writing them (`pricing.ok1`, `import pricing.{ok1};`; there is no wildcard import), so its own `ok1` never clashes with the new one; the loader (`unit::load`) reads imports and never importers, and `query::Db::front` is memoized by the unit's text alone, so counting importers would give one text two repairs and break the agreement of batch and single-file checking. Comments at `presburger::free_names` and `front::linear_questions`; test `l01_38_presburger::checker::the_split_repair_in_an_imported_unit_ignores_the_names_its_importers_define` (pricing alone and imported in all three forms by an app that defines `ok1`, `ok2`: same refusal; the repair followed as printed loads with no problem, `pricing.ok1` and `p.ok2` resolve to `pricing`, bare `ok1`, `ok2` to the app's own definitions).
- TRIVIAL-walk-picks (COMPLEXITY C32 (1) and F131; no spec change; tests only, `tests/steps/l22_08_vacuity/`; own attempt): where the walk of a shared-field atom splits a node n against a node w of a field f, the lists of the choices whose children can hold a pair are made for all the pairs of classes of w and n's children of f together: those children's own children are indexed once for (n, f) by choice and key, and each live child of w is looked up there, so a batch costs w's live children plus the choices it keeps, times a log; it runs only when the lists not made yet would cost more one by one. On the three families of the row (alternate, tagged, rotations) at m = 64: 141,970, 105,874 and 63,442 steps (387,214, 367,246 and 321,102 before; now 5 to 6.4 times the pairs), 132, 87 and 76 million instructions (156, 93 and 81). Other pinned step counts gain the classes counted at each split: the d-family 5 d^2 + 10 d, the cut family 18 k + 46, the joint family 20 m^2 + 34 m + 21, brief, wide and ne 3 m + 10, 3 m + 1 and 2 m + 5 more; pairs and runs unchanged. Left open, plan row TRIVIAL-walk-frontier: when n's children of f lie below fields of their own (`q_j(h(..))`), each pair of classes still makes its list alone (446,482 steps for 25,090 pairs at m = 64). 27 tests, `--only l22_08_vacuity`

## Refusal census (2026-11-12, REFUSAL-census-now)

A first count of the checker's refusals on main 7db90f5d6, rerun unchanged on 0c230df62. Kept current by the step test `m0_12_refusal_census`, whose snapshots list every refusal with its program, site, severity, kinds and reason, so a refusal that appears or disappears fails it. Item REFUSAL-census reruns the count through L6.

**Corpus.** Every enabled fence of the spec, the examples and the README: 0 refusals. Every step unit `tests/steps/**/*.zed`: 0 refusals. Every distinct unit the step tests compiled (59,664, written out by a temporary hook in `ast::unit_all_errors` during a run of the step tests and removed before the commit): 120 units hold a refusal; they are `tests/steps/m0_12_refusal_census/programs.txt`, censused in 12 pieces, the longest 22 s at load 53. 10 units were not censused, since each runs past 300 s alone in a debug build at load 45, all scaling or depth tests: `l01_08_parser::deep::deep_powers` (1 unit), `l01_14_name_resolution::above::checking_the_order_of_a_block_or_a_list_scales` (2 units of 2.8 and 3.8 MB), `l01_38_presburger` (4 units of 4 to 76 KB from its generated families) and `l01_38_presburger::one_scope::the_relations_of_a_chain_{dividing_by_its_argument,calling_an_integer_function}_scale` (3 units).

**Totals per kind** (lines of the census; a line is one diagnostic): Growth 1332, Tie 23, Shadows 16, Unchosen 14, Holes 10, Unordered 9, Disjuncts 3, ArrowMeet 3, MorphismSplit 2, TupleSplit 1, ArrowSplit 1, Other 0. Fork, Residues, SharedCells, NoWitness, Group, PowerMemory, FunctionPairs, PolySums and PolyExponent: 0. Of the 1,414 lines, 279 reject their unit and 1,135 are warnings. Unchosen (`ty.rs` `unchosen_text`) and FunctionPairs (`ty.rs` `Forms::tie`) are kinds the code has that the brief did not name.

| l01_38_presburger | 52 | Tie 19, Growth 19, Shadows 14, Unordered 6, Disjuncts 3 | 61 / 0 | hand-made families and random systems, except the three realistic programs below |

**Realistic programs** (programs a person would plausibly write; each is a test function, so its unit is rejected, since the checker works out the condition of every test function):

1. Unordered, 2 diagnostics: `ok(i, n) = 0 <= bitAnd(i, n) && bitAnd(i, n) <= n && bitAnd(i, n) <= i;` (`l01_39a_bit_words::rung2::a_bit_and_of_nonnegative_operands_is_at_most_each`).
2. Unordered: `ok(a: int, b: int) = (if a > 0 { 2 } else { 0 }) + (if b > 0 { 2 } else { 0 }) != 3;` (`l01_38_presburger::ladder::conditionals_are_refused_raw_and_proved_once_joined`, and four renamings and reorderings in `the_verdict_does_not_depend_on_order_or_names`).
3. Unordered: `ok(x: int, y: int) = 0 <= x && x <= 9 && 0 <= y && y <= 9 && 1 <= x + y && x + y <= 10 && (x <= 2 || x >= 7) && (y <= 2 || y >= 7);` (`l01_38_presburger::checker::following_each_repair_of_the_menu_makes_the_program_check`).
4. Disjuncts: four values each in 0..2 and pairwise `!=` (the pigeonhole case, same test).

**Ranking of refusal kinds by realistic programs hit:** Unordered 3 (7 units with the renamings), Disjuncts 1, every other kind 0. Every other refusal comes from a hand-made adversarial family, a random seed or a generated scaling input. `wt/refusal-sightings.md` held no sightings before this count; the four programs above are now in it.

**Not covered.** The units the step tests compiled were captured on 7db90f5d6; a refusal in a unit a later commit adds to a step test's own code shows only when the capture is run again (item REFUSAL-census). Negative control, run once: a `.zed` step unit with an Unordered refusal moved `step_units` by "Unordered: 2" and failed it.

One cause: each move of a name's interval, mostly in the copies of the scope `cases` makes for the arms of a disjunction, projects again every part that mentions the name (`Scope::project_block` wakes `due_users`), near k parts each time, almost none of which changes; projections grow near k^1.7 to k^1.9 while `Scope::project_part` stays 69 to 100 per cent of the run. stair_holes also costs near k per projection (the holes of `x`). Waking only the parts whose result can change needs, per part, the ends of its names its result depends on; a part whose base holds a constraint on several names, or whose names have holes, has no such ends. coordkk, of the same row, is fixed (COMPLEXITY.md PERF-l139-due). After XR-l139-family (three rounds, done 2026-11-14: f9936c4fe, fe5b3e683, 1aff02482, 16fe26be8), cuts, boxstar, coordmix_floor, star_extra, chain, hopb and hoponb are back as benchmarks in `tests/steps/l01_39_reduced_product/families/bench.rs` (hopb 9.85, hoponb 9.87 times the instructions at 8n through `tools/run_tests.sh --bench`); persist stays deferred at 11.31 (PERF-l139-persist-due), hopb and hoponb stay over 9 (PERF-l139-hopb-wakes).

- Found by PROJECT-box-half-open (2026-11-10), not fixed (COMPLEXITY.md PROJECT-box-half-open, open points): (i) twin quotient and remainder definitions, `i == 3 * q0 + q1 && 0 <= q1 <= 2` written twice, are not merged, since that conjunct defines two atoms (s22 row 1000 case 3640); (ii) projecting one nested chain of `abs` definitions with no twins takes 0.2 s at 16 levels and 3.4 s at 64, about n² (pre-existing), and twin chains, which main refused in about 47 ms, now reach it (1.9 s at 32 levels, 6.6 s at 64); fixed by PROJECT-abs-chain-quadratic (2026-11-10, COMPLEXITY.md C47); (iii) ten boxes of s22's transfer before (cases 366, 463, 482, 1264, 1420, 1930, 2087, 2314, 3817, 3897) were marked exact though each holds 1 to 17 values that are not points, the same on main; fixed by S22-exact-mislabel (2026-11-10).

- Found by PROJECT-abs-chain-quadratic (2026-11-10), not fixed (COMPLEXITY.md C47): projections still above O(n log n), the same on main: a chain `p(k) == max(p(k-1) - 1, 0)` (0.054 s at 64 levels, 0.79 s at 256), a tree of `abs` (2.7 s at 32 nodes, 14.1 s at 64), two chains that differ from level n/2 (6.3 s at 64, 24.0 s at 128). The cost is in `settle`: (a) a run of removals against the order of the disjunctions moves one disjunction per round; (b) the base is solved whole again for each disjunct that joins it when no local repair follows it (`solve` 57% and `own_repair` 38% of the instructions on the max chain at 128); (c) the twin disjunctions `twins_merged` leaves are not removed as duplicates. A complete fix re-tests, when a disjunct joins the base, only the disjunctions that share an atom with it, and solves only the part of the base the new disjunct reaches.
