- Found by LOAD-chain (2026-11-07): the linear questions of a chain of tests `p{i}(x: int) = p{i-1}(x: x) && x > i` take Θ(n²) time: the question of `p{i}` is a relation of i constraints, so the n questions hold n²/2, and each is read and decided on its own (2.23G, 8.91G and 35.7G instructions at 200, 400 and 800 functions; main 3.16G, 12.5G and 49.4G). Memory is linear (35.9 MB at 800). Fixed by LOAD-chain-share (ready on wt/load-chain-share): each relation holds its callee's as a shared part and is decided from its answers, O(n) on this chain; the classes left open are in COMPLEXITY.md LOAD-chain-share.

- Found by GROUP-oracle (2026-11-05): `Type::verdict` refuses (`NoWitness`) inhabited members of a recursive group whose shortest member is long. The chain group `R_i = (R_j, R0) | (R_{i+1}, #stop)`, `R_{n-1} = (R_j, R0) | #stop`, `j` random, is answered `Inhabited` for each of four seeds at n up to 4, has a refused member for at least two of four seeds at n = 8, and `R0` is refused at n 64, 256, 512 and 2048; its member is the chain `((… (#stop, #stop) …), #stop)`. Inferred cause, not confirmed: `rep` in `types/empty.rs` keeps the `None` of a type whose search met a type still being built (on the path) and reuses it after that type gets a value. The random sweeps meet the same refusals: 85 of 2,905 members the pool shows inhabited (79 in the layered groups). A refusal is never a wrong answer, so no test fails; the fix needs a plan row. Fixed for the chain group by VERDICT-group-share (2026-11-07): the cause was as inferred, and `rep` now seeks such a failure again when the type it read gets a value; every member of a chain group of 512 and 1024 is `Inhabited`. The sweeps' refusals are 84 of the members the pool shows inhabited (79 in the layered groups, unchanged), so the layered groups' refusals have another cause, still open. REP-path-memo (2026-11-07) found three causes, fixed two (the sweeps now assert their counts: 80 refusals, 79 in the layered groups and 1 in the cells groups, none in the X14 or mixed groups) and left these open: a closure whose key type only a search proves empty (`fn[empty] Id`, most of the layered refusals; plan item EMPTY-key-search); a group the decider refuses, where the builder takes a closure as returnable only when its value type is itself being built, so the outcome depends on the order it builds in (inferred inherent: deciding it in general is the mixed fixed point the decider refuses); and, in decided groups, a closure whose value type is a tuple holding a type still being built, such as `(int, R0)` (seeds 864 and 1139 of the mixed generator, seen in a sweep of seeds 300 to 1,500 that is not committed). EMPTY-key-search (2026-11-07) fixed the first: the committed sweeps now refuse 8 members the pool shows inhabited (7 in the layered groups, 1 in the cells groups). In the uncommitted sweep of seeds 300 to 1,500 (54 refusals: layered 34, cells 9, X14 7, mixed 4), 44 are in groups holding `\` or `&` (the second cause), 2 are the third, 7 are in X14 groups, whose cause is not traced (their closures return tuples of closures), and 1 (layered seed 883) is a key type whose emptiness reads a type still being decided, proved only when a phase of the search ends (COMPLEXITY.md K60, kept). TESTS-l01_23-group-oracle-sweep (2026-11-12) committed that sweep with every refusal listed: on main it refuses 35 members the pool shows inhabited (layered 33, cells 2, none in X14 or mixed) and 4 it leaves open (layered); each layered one is or reads a function type whose value type is a pair of itself and a difference of two definitions, such as layered seed 799's `R3 = (int) -> (R3, (R2 \ R0))`. Plan row GROUP-layered-nowitness owns these refusals; `group_oracle.rs` `layered_seed_799_member_3_is_inhabited`, ignored with that ID, fails with `Refused(NoWitness)` (TESTS-ignores-and-owners, 2026-11-12).

- T12 was removed on 2026-11-05 by the author's order. The performance rule at the top of `docs/plan_dag.md` replaces it: every code agent passes an O(1), O(n) or O(n log n) performance test, and O(n²) or worse needs the author's approval. SCALE-cover holds T12's tool and its check of code already written.

- After L1.37a, the feature build (`--features short-addresses`) fails tests that check the hash itself, by design, and these run in the full build only: `l01_32` `facet_order` (equal and different addresses), `stability::the_address_is_pinned`, `fuzz::the_key_agrees_with_the_address`; `m0_07` `rules::the_version_tag_separates_rule_sets`, `alpha::addresses_agree_with_an_independent_alpha_equivalence_test`; `m0_11` `units::the_address_is_pinned`. Some scaling tests also exceed their limits in that build. Measured after repair #1, which keeps the lowering's nodes of one key in a map ordered by shape: `l01_33` 43 of 43 and `l01_37a_short_addresses` 16 of 16 pass there (the earlier chain failed 3 and 2 of them, on bytes allocated, 24.1 to 34.0 times against 24); still failing are `l01_20` `scaling::the_term_of_every_fact_scales`, `m0_09` `provenance::the_check_for_repeated_addresses_on_a_chain_of_products_scales`, `l01_26` `literals::adopting_the_literals_of_a_deep_tuple_scales` and `l01_23` `listing::taking_k_values_costs_k_times_the_depth`, and the rest of `l01_23` passes the 60 s limit there. None of these lower ZIR. Profiled (perf, 8-bit build) for the `l01_26` and `l01_23` tests: most cycles go to comparing type contents where the 8-bit digests tie (`Ord` of `Type`, `Tuples`, `Lits`, `Atoms`, of ordered sets of `Value`, and `bdd::order`), so each comparison costs the size of the types instead of O(1). The `l01_20` and `m0_09` failures and the deep-stack tests of `l01_16`, `l01_31`, `l01_34` (which timed out before repair #1, not rerun since) are not profiled; their cause is inferred to be the same. The stack overflows of `l01_22` `surface::the_text_of_a_type_shared_n_deep_scales` and `l01_23` `listing::finiteness_scales_with_the_types_not_the_values` were the order of types recursing once per level of tied digests, fixed by SHORT-stack-l01_22 (COMPLEXITY.md K48); both now run past 60 s there, as a chain n deep costs about n² to build when its levels tie (1,000 levels in 6 s, debug). Measured on 2026-11-04 after that fix, test by test under 60 s, the short build fails in `l01_23` the same tests as before it: `listing::taking_k_values_costs_k_times_the_depth`, `scaling::a_decision_tree_is_decided_in_polynomial_time`, `scaling::a_tuple_that_shapes_hold_only_together_is_checked_in_the_size_of_the_union`, `scaling::nested_tuples_scale`, `x13::e4b_scales` and `x13::the_union_of_nth_from_end_is_built_in_its_size` fail, and `cells::a_decision_tree_is_decided_in_time_linear_in_its_size`, `x13::the_union_of_nth_from_end_is_decided_in_its_size` and `listing::finiteness_scales_with_the_types_not_the_values` run past 60 s, with the 98 others passing; `l01_22` passes 40 of 41 and `l01_26` 195 of 196. The local suite runs `l01_37a_short_addresses` and `l01_37_oracle` in that build (tools/run_tests.sh, `short-*` pieces, built in a clone of `build/cargo` mounted for each run at `build/short-clone/cargo` and kept until `--short-clone-remove` or the deletion of the checkout; until BUILD-short-clone, the target `build/short`).
- Resolved after L1.37a by BDD-atom-order: the printed text of a type no longer follows the BDD atom order, so `(| (tuple 0 #a0) (tuple 1 #a1)) - (tuple 1 _)` prints `(| (& (tuple 0 #a0) (! (tuple 1 _))) (& (tuple 1 #a1) (! (tuple 1 _))))` and `((0, #a0) | (1, #a1)) \ (1, _)` in both builds, and the case is in `record::printed_types` (COMPLEXITY.md K47).
- After L1.37a, an import's `pin` is compared by address alone: there are no contents to fall back on, since the pinned unit may be absent. Not checked at L1. The weak topological order (`wto`) breaks ties by address and then by form, so its order differs between the two builds; its results do not (`m0_05` passes in both).
- After L1.17a: `Ord` on numbers cannot fail, so after a refused comparison it gives the order of the normal forms until the run stops with the refusal. A sort inside one run that meets both a refused pair and the same pair by value could see an inconsistent order; the run still stops with the refusal, but the sort's result before that is not specified.
- The instruction count of `zed_tests::scaling` does not show the order of large copies done
  by vector moves (T11-fix-rest, F46): the old `resolve` took 10.2 times the instructions at
  8 times the size, but 51.8 times the processor time. A scaling test of code whose cost is
  copying memory needs a second measure, such as bytes allocated or copied (ledger item
  SCALE-bytes). Done: SCALE-bytes (3fa1fdc) checks bytes allocated next to instructions.
- After T14-occ (COMPLEXITY.md K25): `Provenance::origins` reads a family entry by entry when
  no family it was made from, or made from it, has been read, at the cost of the set of
  failures each entry holds, so `n` entries holding one set of `m` failures cost `n·m` (no
  worse than before). Fixed by PROV-family-entries: entries holding one set are counted once,
  and a changed entry is compared shallowly; entries whose sets grow by one failure each are
  still `O(n²)` (K25); fixed by PROV-union-growing. Its oldest-first pass read every fact `i` reaches, so a failure read beside a large value holding none cost that value's parts; fixed by PROV-oldest-failing. Since ADDR-keys (COMPLEXITY.md K40), `deep.rs` and `origins` key shared
  sequences by `Items::id`, not by address.
- From OSP-diag: (a) Fixed by OSP-neglit: `-1.abs`, the case of the rejection row "Prefix `-` on a
  numeric literal's postfix chain", is rejected by the AST builder. (b) Fixed in repair #1: the rows "Named argument before a positional one"
  and "`positional` parameter after a named one" are set by the AST builder. (c) The
  `for T in …` clause DESIGN decides for printed bounds is not in the `Type` grammar. (d) The
  printed-type check leaves out what type syntax cannot state: families, payloads, the names
  of positional parameters, defaults, needs, ownership and data. (e) Features `printed-types`
  and `counts` are on in any build that includes `zed-tests`, since cargo unifies features in
  a workspace build; a release build of `zedc` alone has both off. A `default-members` list
  without `tests` would fix a plain `cargo build` but not `cargo build --workspace`, which
  builds every member; a release is built per binary (`cargo build --release -p zed-native`, which builds `zedc` and
  the runtime library `libzed_native.a` that `zedc build` links).

- Corpus outputs that rest on rules the spec has not fixed yet; each is a choice stated in
  the program's `ref/NN.py`, to be revisited at the step that fixes the rule: the `.window`
  signature and late-drop rule (programs 17, 18, 29; step L7.5), where a parse error is
  reported (7, 30), `serialize` writing no whitespace, `++` on int-keyed sets reading in key
  order, `zip` keeping the overlap of two rank ranges (25), stdin keyed by rank from 0.
  The programs are only parsed and layer-checked so far, not type-checked or run.
- Programs 14 and 15 are labeled L7 for incremental reuse (L7.6), though their syntax only
  reaches L6.

- Apply the batch of resolutions from the six-part read of DESIGN.md (scan files in the
  session scratchpad), prose and grammar together, before the steps they affect.

## Postmortem amendments (spec commit after 678e2d1)

The postmortem of related languages (array, dataflow, Datalog and incremental languages; report kept outside the repo) proposed nine amendments. Applied to DESIGN.md:
- A3: `@export("c", "symbol")` lets C call pure Zed functions (sec:ffi; tested in L7.4).
- A1: `zed build --explain-plan` (L5.10).
- A2: a lowering stays within a constant factor of `f::cost`; `@cost(depth: …)`.
- A6: recompute or incremental is chosen per wave by cost; the L7 gate adds a 50%-dirty check.
- A7: the L5 ratios are one core against one core, and efficiency is measured against the Rust baseline. L5.14 now agrees with the gate table.

Not applied:
- A4 (name a first domain): a product decision with no effect on what is built.
- A5 (license): the repo already has LICENSE; the choice belongs to the owner.
- A8 (two-process test at L7): distribution is post-v1 in sec:targets.
- A9 (count programs needing generations): no decision depends on the count.

## M0.3 — desugaring rules (done, in the spec)

The spec's sec:grammar now has a `desugar` fence with one rule per syntactic production (107), and the spec repo's `tools/grammar/check.py` checks that rules and productions match one to one. A negative control (an extra rule and a duplicate) is caught. Nothing in this repo changes until the L1 elaborator, which implements these rules. Decisions:
- `&&` and `||` desugar to `if`, not to the strict primitives; the spec calls them selection nodes that short-circuit observationally.
- Recursion enters at L6. A recursive function is the definedness fix over its parameter domain, evaluated on demand. The M0.9 evaluator computes that fix over a finite domain only; the L1/L6 interpreter evaluates on demand.
- Kernel primitives the rules name that the M0.9 kernel lacks: `pow` (L1), `range` (L3), and the type test `is` (L1). They are added at those steps.
- `break e`: the step's guard returns `#break(e)` and the loop's result is `e`.
- T14 and T11 findings are now nodes in `docs/plan_dag.md`, with a table placing each finding
  (section "T14 and T11 findings"): T14-bugs-rt, T14-bugs-kernel, T14-value, T14-heap,
  T14-hooks, T14-rope, T14-bring, T14-paths, T14-provenance, T14-low, T14-rest, T11-preimage,
  T11-ty, T11-check, T11-elab. T14 itself blocks nothing; T12 needs every fix node, and
  L1.41 needs T12 (since 4420380, L1.40 needs only T4, ST1 and ST2). Plan only: no code changed.
- `Prim::TupleGet` on a `fix` under construction is a type error, `TupleGet applied to a function`: the Partial case in `Machine::prim` tests only `Prim::Get`, while `elab.rs` gives `v[0]` as `TupleGet`. No term reaches it today, since `elab.rs` makes no `Term::Fix`; the elaboration of definedness `fix` must write `Get` or the case must take both, as the port case does.
